מנוד.def:
ו‎

ו‎, Waw, sixth letter; in modern Hebrew = numeral 6; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

וָ וּ, וְ,‎

demonstrative adverb and

conjunction so, then, and (Phoenician, Moabite, Aramaic ו‎; Arabic ; Ethiopic Assyrian u DlW (but between verbs the usually connective is the enclitic ma KAT2. 508, Dl§§ 82, 150). The use in Hebrew shews that original וְ‎ was not a merely copulative conjunction, but that it possessed a demonstrative force (compare Dr§ 122), which is often perceptible as such, though in other cases, from its being applied to denote mere juxtaposition or connection [compare Greek τε, and Latin tum .... tum = 'both .... and,' both properly demonstratives: Assyrian ma has also a demonstrative force, Dl§ 79], it is less palpable) — וְ‎ before shwa' mobile or a labial is vocalized וּ‎; often before a tone-syll., when the word itself has a disj. accent, וָ‎ (as וַָמתִּי׃‎ Gen 19:19; וָמֵ֖תוּ‎ 33:13; וָמֵ֑ת‎ 44:9; וָחָֽיָה׃‎ Exod 1:16; וָיָ֑מָּה‎ Josh 15:46; וָ֔לֹ֕א‎ 2Sam 13:26; וָאָ֖רֶץ‎ Isa 26:19; וָקָ֔מוּ‎ 49:7; וָחָֽתָּה׃‎ Jer 48:1; וָרָֹע‎ Psa 10:15); especially when it forms with the preceding word a pair, whether of parallel or opposed ideas (as וָכֹה כֹּה‎ Exod 2:12, וָמִ֖י מִי‎ 10:8, וָאָ֑בֶן אֶבֶן‎ Deut 25:13; וָדֹ֑ר דֹּר‎ 32:7 +; וָבֹ֔הוּ תֹּהוּ‎ Gen 1:2, וָרֶמֶ֛שׂ בְּהֵמָה‎ 1:24, וָרָֽע׃ טוֺב‎ 2:19, וָנָ֖ד נָע‎ 4:12, וָלָ֖יְלָה וְיוֺם וָחֹ֛רֶף וְקַיִץ‎ 8:22, וֵָלךְ׃ קַח‎ 12:19, וָאָֽרֶץ׃ שָׁמַיִם‎ 14:19, וָאָ֑תָּה אֲנִי‎ 31:44, וָה֑וּא אֲנִי‎ 41:11, וָשׁוּבוּ עִבְרוּ‎ Exod 32:27, וָהֵ֛ם אַתָּה‎ Num 16:16, וָמֶ֑לָךְ אֱלֹהִים‎ 1Kin 21:13, וָנֶ֖כֶד נִין‎ Isa 14:22, וָשֶׁ֖בֶר שֹׁד‎ 59:7; and often: see more fully Bö§ 600); occasionally also with a conjunctive accent (as לְעֹלָֽם׃ וָשַחי‎ Gen 3:22 compare Lev 18:5, שָׁם וָמַ֣תְנוּ‎ 2Kin 7:4, חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וָאָ֣רֶץ‎ Isa 65:17; Prov 25:3, גָּדוֺל׃ וָשֶשׁבֶר שֹׁ֖ד‎ Jer 48:3, compare 32:29). — וְ‎ is used very freely and widely in Hebrew, but also with much delicacy, to express relations and shades of meaning which Western languages would usually indicate by distinct particles. But in Hebrew particles such as לָכֵן לְמַעַן, בַּעֲבוּר, אוּלָם, אָכֵן, אַךְ, אָז, אוֺ,‎, etc., were reserved for cases in which special emphasis or distinctness was desired: their frequent use was felt instinctively to be inconsistent with the lightness and grace of movement which the Hebrew ear loved; and thus in AV, RV, words like or, then, but, notwithstanding, howbeit, so, thus, therefore, that, constantly appear, where the Hebrew has simply וְ‎.

1 And, connecting both words (see above), and sentences (Gen 1:5 וג קָרָא ׳וְלַחשֶׁךְ‎). When three, four, or more words follow, the conjunction may connect them all, as 7:21; 10:2 (6 t.) 24:35 (7 t.) Josh 7:24 (10 t.) 2Sam 17:28f.: often however it is prefixed only to the last, as Gen 5:32; 10:1; Deut 18:10 etc.; occas. even it connects only the first two, 1Kin 8:47; Isa 1:13; Psa 45:9; Job 42:9. Remarkably, however, וְ‎ as a mere conjunction is, as a rule, not in classical Hebrew attached directly to verbs (especially in the perfect), the construction with וְ‎ consecutive (see

2) being (as in Moabite) preferred: thus וַיִּבֶן יָצָא‎ is said, not וּבָנָה יָצָא‎. Exceptions in classical Hebrew are (a) sometimes where synonyms are coupled, as Num 23:19 וְדִבֶּר ֗֗֗ אָמַר‎, Deut 2:30; Judg 5:26; 1Sam 12:2; Isa 1:2 ורוממתי גדּלתי‎ 2:11; 5:14; 8:8; 19:6; 29:20; (b) isolated cases, difficult to reduce to rule (perhaps sometimes due to textual error), as Gen 28:6; 38:5; Judg 3:23; 7:13; 16:18; 1Sam 1:12; 3:13; 4:19; 5:7; 10:9; 17:38, 48; 25:20 and elsewhere (in other passages, apparently similar, the perfect and וְ‎ has a frequent. force (see 2), as Gen 37:3; Exod 36:29f.; Num 10:17f. 21:15, 20; 1Sam 2:22; 16:14; 17:34f. (see Dr) 27:9; 2Sam 16:13; 17:17, perhaps also Gen 15:6; 21:25; 34:5). In later parts of OT, probably through Aramaic influence, the perfect with simple וְ‎ occurs more frequently: so especially in Ecclesiastes, where it is all but universal (e.g. 2:11-12, 13, 15 etc.). With the imperfect, the simple וְ‎ is not so unidiomatic, even in classical Hebrew (compare 3); see 1:9, 26; 9:27; 17:2; 22:17; 27:29; Exod 23:8 (frequently) 24:7; Num 14:12; Deut 17:13; 30:12-13, Josh 3:13; 7:3; Judg 7:3; 13:8; Isa 5:29; 14:10; often also in Jeremiah, Isa2, Job, Psalms, e.g. 40:30; 41:20 (Dr§ 116: contrast 28:13). See more fully Dr§ 130-4 Ges§ 112. 6. Special senses: —

a. it sometimes = and specially, Gen 3:16; 1Kin 11:1 many strange women, and specially the daughter of Pharaoh, Isa 1:1 Judah and (= and particularly) Jerusalem, 2:1; 9:7; Psa 18:1.

b. and in particular ('und zwar'), and that (explicative), Gen 4:4; Judg 7:22; 1Sam 17:40 וּבַיַּלְקוּט‎, 28:3 in Ramah, and that in his city (unusual: text suspicious), 2Sam 13:20 וְשֹׁמֵמָה‎ and that desolate, Isa 57:11 I have been silent וּמֵעוֺלָם‎ and that from of old, 32:7; Jer 15:13; Amos 3:11 (si vera lectio), 4:10; Zech 9:9b Mal 1:11; Psa 68:10; Prov 3:12; Lam 3:26; Eccl 8:2; Dan 1:3; 8:10; 9:25, 27; Neh 8:13; 1Chr 9:27; 2Chr 8:13; 29:27 (but' even' for ו‎, before ל‎ and infinitive, e.g. in Isa 44:28; Jer 17:10; 19:12, is wrong; see Ew§ 351 c, Dr§ 206).

c. sometimes it introduces an idea which so exceeds or adds to what has preceded, that it is nearly equivalent to also, 1Sam 25:43; 1Kin 2:22 ask also the kingdom for him; unusually Hosea 8:6 והוא מישׂראל כי‎ for of Israel is it also, Eccl 5:6 והבלים‎ (see De) 2Chr 27:5 (but see ᵐ5‎). Or it may be rendered yea: so especially in the ascending numerations 3-4 Amos 1:3, 6, 9, 11, 13; 2:1, 4, 6; Prov 30:18, 21, 29, 6-7 6:16; Job 5:19, 7-8 Micah 5:4 — the first number being aggravated, or augmented, by a higher. In one idiom וּגְבוּל‎, occurring in geographic descriptions, it is used peculiarly, seemingly = at the same time: Num 34:6 and as for the western border, וּגְבוּל הַגָּדוֺל הַיָּם לָכֶם וְהָיָה‎ the great sea shall be to you also (German 'zugleich') a border, Deut 3:16 וּגְבוּל הַנַּחַל תּוֺךְ‎ the middle of the stream being at the same time the border, 3:17; Josh 13:23, 27; 15:12, 47 (but these, except Num 34:6, might be cases of 5c γ).

d. it connects alternative cases, so that it = or: Exod 20:10, 17; 21:16 he that stealeth a man בְיָדוֺ וְנִמְצָא וּמְכָרוֺ‎ and selleth him, and (= or if) he be found in his hand, 21:17; Lev 21:14; 22:23-24, Prov 29:9 (Fl Ew RV: whether . . . or) Job 31:13, 16, 26, etc.

e. it connects contrasted ideas, where in our idiom the contrast would be expressed explicitly by but; in such cases prominence is usually given to the contrasted idea by its being placed immediately after the conjunction: Gen 2:17 but of the tree of the knowledge . . . thou shalt not eat, 4:2, 5; 6:8; 17:21; 31:10 etc., 1Kin 2:26; 10:7; 11:32, 34; 15:14; Prov 10:1-2, 3, 4 + often; even after לֹא‎ (where כִּי‎ or אִם כִּי‎ might be expected), as Gen 42:10; Exod 21:18; Lev 26:45; Deut 11:11; Judg 19:12; 1Kin 3:11.

f. it introduces a contrasted idea in such a way as to suggest a question, especially before a pronoun, Judg 14:16 I told it not to my father or my mother, אַגִּיד וְלָךְ‎ and shall I told it unto thee? 2Sam 11:11; Jer 25:29 תִנָּקוּ הִנָּקֵה וְאַתֶּם‎ and shall ye be guiltless? 45:5; Ezek 20:31; 33:25b Jonah 4:11. So the וְ‎ consecutive and perfect (see 2a), Exod 5:5 וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּם‎ and will ye make them rest from their burdens? Num 16:10 וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם‎ and seek ye the priesthood also? 1Sam 25:11; Isa 66:9; Psa 50:21 and shall I keep silence? Job 32:16 (compare Dr§ 119 γ).

g. attaching a fresh subj. (or object) to a clause already grammatically complete, it = and also, Gen 2:9b Num 16:2, 18 and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, ואהרן ומשׁה‎ and Moses and Aaron (stood also), 16:27; Exod 35:22; Judg 6:5; Gen 1:16; b 12:17; 44:2; 46:15; Exod 29:3; Jer 32:29 (compare DrSm. i. 6, 11, & p. 293): when the idea thus attached is subordinate, or not logically embraced in the principal predicate, it approximates to the Arabic or 'waw of association' (followed by an accusative: WAG ii. § 37), Est 4:16 אָצוּם וְנַעֲרֹתַי אֲנִי‎ I will fast (singular) and (= with) my maidens, Exod 21:4; 1Sam 25:42; 29:10b (but insert here אַתָּה‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Sam 12:30 (but read וּבָהּ‎, as 1Chr 20:2) 1Sam 20:10; Neh 6:12; Gen 4:20; Isa 42:5; Jer 19:1 (but read מזקני וְלָקַחְתָּ֫‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Chr 2:3; 13:11; compare Jer 22:7 (וְכֵלָיו אִישׁ‎), Job 41:12. Whether Isa 48:16 וְרוּחוֺ‎ belongs here, is dubious

h. וְ‎ repeated = both . . . and (but גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎) is more usual in this sense); Gen 34:28; Num 9:14; Josh 9:23; 2Sam 5:8 (text dubious), Isa 16:5; 38:15; Jer 13:14; 21:6; 32:14 (text dubious) 32:20; 40:8; Psa 76:7; Job 34:29; Dan 8:13; Neh 12:28.

i. a repetition of the same word with וְ‎ interposed expresses (a) diversity (rare), Deut 25:13 וָאֶבֶן אֶבֶן‎ a weight and a weight, i.e. different weights (explained by וּקְטַנָּה גְּדֹלָה‎), 25:14; Prov 20:23; Psa 12:3 וָלֵב בְּלֵב‎ with a heart and a heart = with a double heart, 1Chr 12:33 וָלֵב לֵב בְּלֹא‎; (b) distribution (except in וָדֹר דֹּר‎ Deut 32:7; Isa 13:20 +?Intr. 505) Psa 87:5; 1Chr 26:13 וָשָֽׁעַר׃ לְשַׁעַר‎ = for every gate, 28:14 (twice in verse); 2Chr 8:14; 34:13; 35:15; Ezra 10:14 וָעִיר עִיר זִקְנֵי‎ elders of every city, Neh 13:24; Est 1:8, 22 (twice in verse); 2:12; 3:4, 12 (4 t. in verse); 8:9 (twice in verse); strengthened by כָּלֿ‎2Chr 11:12 ועיר עיר בכל‎ in every several city, 19:5; 28:25; 31:19; 32:28; Est 2:11 ויום בכליֿום‎, 3:14; 4:3; 8:11, 13, 17 (twice in verse); 9:21, 27, 28; Psalm 45:18; Psa 145:13 (common in post-Biblical Hebrew, especially with כל‎).

j. it is used in the formulation of proverbs (the Vav adaequationis, הִשְׁתַּוָּאָה וָו‎) as Prov 17:3; 25:3, 20, 25 cold waters to a thirsty soul and good news from a far country (i.e. they are like each other), 26:3, 9, 14, 20; 27:21; Eccl 5:2; 7:1; 8:8; compare 9:11; Psa 19:5; 125:2; Job 14:11f.; 14:19 (compare in Arabic 'every man and his cares [accusative],' 'every thing and its price,' i.e. they go together: 'merchants and dogs [accusative] of Seleucia,' i.e. they are like one another: see FlKl. Schr. iii. 535 f.). More rarely in the opposite order, 5:7; 12:11. But 1Sam 12:15b cannot be thus explained: read with וּבְמַלְכְּכֶם ᵐ5‎, and see Dr.

k. in circumstantial clauses וְ‎ introduces a statement of the concomitant conditions under which the action denoted by the principal verb takes place: in such cases, the relation expressed by וְ‎ must often in English be stated explicitly by a conjunction, as when, since, seeing, though, etc., as occasion may require. So very often, as Gen 11:4 let us build a tower בַשָּׁמַיִם וְראֹשׁוֺ‎ and its top in the heavens (= with its top in etc.), 18:12 shall I have pleasure, זָקֵן וַאדֹנִי‎ and my lord is old (= my lord being old)? Judg 16:15 How sayest thou, I love thee, אִתִּי אֵין וְלִבְּךָ‎ and (= when) thy heart is not with me? and especially with a person pronoun, Gen 15:2 what wilt thou give me עֲרִירִי הֹלֵךְ וְאָנֹכִי‎ and I (= the case being that I) am going hence childless? 18:13; 20:3 lo, thou wilt die because of the woman thou hast taken בָּֽעַל׃ בְּעֻלַת וְהִוא‎ = seeing she is married, 24:62 ישֵׁב וְהוּא‎ = since or for he was dwelling (different from וַיֵּשֶׁב‎ = and he proceeded to dwell), 26:27 וְאַתֶּם‎ seeing ye hate me, Judg 13:9 and came to her ישֶׁבֶת וְהִיא‎ = as she was sitting, 1Sam 18:23; 1Kin 19:19 +? Psa 72:12 the afflicted לוֺ וְאֵיןעֹֿזֵר‎ and (= when) he has no helper (compare Job 29:12), Job 104:25 מִסְמָּר וְאֵין‎, Job 105:34; 5:9. See more fully Dr§ 156-60 Ges§ 141, R 2. (The analogous use of the is very common in Arabic: Wii. § 183.) Introducing an appeal to a fact confirmatory of some statement or promise, it almost = as truly as (compare Ew§ 340 c) Hosea 12:6 and J. is God of hosts, J. is his name! Joel 4:20; Amos 9:5-6 Isa 51:15 and I [who promise this] am J. thy God, who . . . . ! Jer 29:23; Psa 89:38b (compare in Qoran the frequently 'And God is .. . . . [the mighty, the merciful, etc.]').

2 The ו‎ consecutive (formerly called the Waw 'conversive'); —

a. with the

imperfect (וַּ‎ with following daghesh; before וָ א,‎), as וַיּאֹמֶר‎ properly = and he proceeded to say, chiefly in contin. of a preceding perfect tense (so Moabite);

b. with the

perfect (וְ‎, — in 1 & 2 singular, the tone, with certain exceptions [see Dr§ 110], being thrown forward to the ultima), as וְיָָֽשַׁבְתָּ֫‎ properly so [namely, as limited by a verb, or other term, preceding] hadst thou sat, chiefly in continuation of a preceding imperfect tense, in its various senses of future, jussive, or frequentative. Thefurther analysis of these idioms belongs to the grammar; see on a DrCh. vi., Ges§ 111, and on

b DrCh. viii. Ges§ 112. Here it must suffice to note — (a) ו‎ consecutive (especially with the imperfect) frequently couples two verbs in such a manner that the first, indicating the general character of the action, receives its closer definition in the second: in such cases, the first may often be represented in English by an adverb, as Gen 26:18 וַיַּחְמֹּר וַיָּשָׁב‎ and he turned and dug = and he dug again; so often; and similarly with הוֺסִיף‎ 25:1, מִהַר‎ 24:18, הוֺאִיל‎ Josh 7:7, etc.; more exceptionally, Gen 30:27; Est 8:6, and (not consecutive) Gen 47:6; Job 23:3; Song 2:3; Lam 3:26 (see Ges§ 120, 2 a; compare in Syriac Nö§ 335-6. In Arabic the stronger form of the conjugation here corresponds: Wii. § 140). (b) וַּ ‎ with the imperfect sometimes expresses a contrast = and yet, Gen 32:31 I have seen God face to face וַתִּנָּצֵל‎ and yet my soul is delivered, Deut 4:33; 2Sam 3:8; 19:29; Isa 51:12; Psa 73:14; 144:3; Job 10:8 + (compare Dr§ 74 β). (c) there is a tendency in the later books of the OT to use the perfect with simple וְ‎, where the classical language would employ the imperfect with וַּ ‎ (compare above

1); so especially in Ecclesiastes, where וַּ ‎ occurs thrice only, Job 1:17; 4:1, 7. (d) a double perfect with ו‎ consecutive is sometimes used, informally but neatly, with a hypothetical force; thus (a) in past or present time Exod 16:21 וְנָמָֽס׃ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְחַם‎ and the sun used to be warm, and it used to melt = and if (or when) the sun was warm, it melted, 33:10; 1Kin 18:10; Jer 18:4, 8 וְנִחַמְתִּ֫י וְֹשָׁב‎ = and if it turns, I repent, 20:9 (see RV); (β) in future time, Gen 44:22 ומת אביו ועזב‎ and he will leave his father, and he will die = and if he leaves his father, he will die, 33:13; 42:38; Exod 4:14; 12:13; 1Sam 16:2; 19:3; Ezek 33:3; 39:15 etc. (Dr§ 147-9, Ges§ 159. 2 e).

3 With a

voluntative (cohortative or jussive) וְ‎ expresses an intention, that or so that (an elegancy by which the too frequent use of לְמַעַן‎ or בַּעֲבוּר‎ is avoided): Exod 10:17 entreat God, וְיָסֵר‎ so may he remove (= that he may remove) this death, Gen 27:4 and bring it me וְאֹכֵ֑לָה‎ so let me eat (= that I may eat); and without the modal form being externally indicated, Exod 14:1 speak . . . וְיָשֻׁבוּ‎ that they return, 14:15; and often Sts. even of past time, as 1Kin 13:33 whom he would, he consecrated וִיהִי‎ that there might be priests of the high places, 2Kin 19:25; Isa 25:9 a Lam 1:19. After a negative, Psa 51:18 thou desirest not sacrifice, וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה‎ so [= in that case] would I give it (or, that I might give it), 55:13 וְאֶשָּׂא‎ so could I bear it (or, that I might bear it), Isa 53:2 RVm Num 23:19; Jer 5:28 RV. Sts. also before an imperative, Gen 12:2 and be (= that thou mayest be) a blessing, 2Sam 21:3 +. See more fully Dr§ 59-65, Ges§ 108. 2; 109. 2; 110. 2. (In Arabic with the subjunctive is used similarly: Wii. § 15 d.) A volunt. is also sometimes attached by וְ‎ to a preceding volunt. or imperative, so as to form a virtually hypothetical sentence, as Gen 42:18 וִחְיוּ עֲשׂוּ זֹאת‎ = if you do this, you shall live, 30:28; 34:12; Prov 3:9f. 4:4, 8; Isa 55:2: see Dr§ 152.

4 It expresses often an informal inference, or consequence, so, then, especially at the beginning of a speech: Gen 27:8; Psa 2:10 and often וְעַתָּה‎ now, therefore; וְלָמָּה‎ and וּמַדּוּעַ‎ why, then? Gen 29:25; Num 12:8; 16:3 +; Exod 2:20 וְאַיּוֺ‎ where, then, is he? Gen 34:21; 1Sam 15:14; 26:22 וְיַעֲבֹר‎ let, then, . . . come over, 2Sam 24:3; 2Kin 4:41 קֶמַח וּקְחוּ‎ then bring meal, Ezek 18:32. So the וְ‎ consecutive and the perfect, as Deut 2:4 וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם‎ take heed, therefore, 4:15; 7:9 וְיָָֽדַעְתָּ֫‎ know, therefore, 30:19; 1Sam 6:5; 1Kin 2:6; Ruth 3:9; Josh 15:19; Isa 40:6b (Dr§ 119 δ).

5 ו‎ introduces the predicate or apodosis: namely

a. וְ‎ consecutive and the Perfect — in answer to אִם‎ or כִּי‎ constantly, as Exod 19:5; 23:22 if thou hearkenest to my voice, וְאָֽיַבְתִּ֫י‎ then am I (= I will be) enemy to thy enemies (see Dr§ 136-8); after the casus pendens, 12:44 every servant that is bought for money, וּמַלְתָּ֫ה‎ thou shalt circumcise him, etc. Num 14:31; 24:24; 1Sam 25:27; 2Sam 14:10 he that spake unto thee, אֵלַי וַהֲבֵאתוֺ‎ so hast thou brought him (= thou shalt bring him) unto me, Isa 9:4; 56:6f. +; Exod 12:15; 31:14; Deut 17:12 +; after various time-determinations, as Gen 3:5 in the day of your eating from it וְנִפְקְחוּ‎ then shall your eyes be opened, Exod 16:6 וִידַעְתֶּם עֶרֶב‎ at even, then shall ye know, 16:7; 32:34; 2Sam 15:10; 1Kin 13:31 אֹתִי וּקְבַרְתֶּם בְּמוֺתִי‎ when I die, so ye shall bury me, etc., + often; after conjs., as כִּי‎ Gen 29:15, יַעַן‎ 1Kin 20:28; Isa 3:16f., תַּחַת‎ 60:15, etc., (see Dr§ 123).

b. וַּ ‎ consecutive and the imperfect (but much less frequently than the perfect), as Gen 30:30 the little that thou hadst, וַיִּפְרֹץ‎ it hath increased, Exod 9:21; 2Sam 4:10; 1Kin 9:20f. 15:13 +; after time-determinations, Gen 22:4 on the third day וַיִּשָּׂא‎ then Abraham lifted up his eyes, 19:15; 27:34; 37:18; 1Sam 6:6; 12:8; Isa 6:1; Hosea 11:1 when Israel was a child, וָאֹהֲבֵהוּ‎ then I loved him, +; occasionally after conjunctions, as כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ Exod 16:34, יַעַן‎ 1Sam 15:23, לְמַעַן‎ Isa 45:4, אִם‎ Psa 59:16 (Dr§ 127).

c. in other cases (not 'consecutive') — all more or less uncommon: namely a. וְ‎ closely joined to the imperfect Gen 13:9 if to the left, וְאֵימִינָה‎ then I will take the right (compare 2Sam 12:8) Exod 12:3 on the 10th of the month וְיִקְחוּ‎ then let them take, Num 16:5; Isa 43:4; Hosea 4:6; 10:10; Psa 69:33; Job 15:17; 2Sam 22:41; Prov 23:24 Kt (Dr§ 125); β. separated from the verb, Exod 8:22; Lev 7:16 יֵאָכֵל וְהַנּוֺתָר וּמִמָּחֳרָת‎ and on the morrow, then the remainder shall be eaten, Josh 3:3; 1Kin 8:32; Isa 8:7; 48:7; Job 14:7; 20:18; b 23:12; 25:5; 32:14 +; γ. without a verb, Gen 40:9 וְהִנֵּה בַּחֲלֹמִי‎ in my dream, behold, a vine was before me, 40:16; 2Sam 23:3f.; Prov 10:25, and the extreme cases 2Sam 15:34 thy father's slave, מֵאָז וַאֲנִי‎ I was that of old, — but now עַבְדְּךָ וַאֲנִי‎ well, I will be thine, Isa 34:12 (si vera lectio), Job 4:6b דְּרָכֶיךָ וְתֹם תִּקְוָָֽתְךָ‎ thy confidence — it is the uprightness of thy ways, 36:26 חֵקֶר וְלֹא שָׁנָיו מִסְמַּר‎ Ges. seine Jahre, da ist kein Zählen (compare Dr§ 124-5, 128-9). — With 4, 5 compare the Arabic , Wi. § 366 b, 367 c; ii. § 187; Dr§ 185 end.

Neh 10:34, compare Lev 6:13; Num 4:16 (all cases under

H2680. chatsi

Hammanachti מָנַחְתִּי‎ adjective, of a people perhaps from foregoing, only with article as collective noun הַמּ ׳חֲצִי‎ 1Chr 2:54 of a Judaean tribe (ᵐ5‎ Μαλαθει, A ᵐ5‎L Μαναθ(ι)); so read also probably for הַמְּנֻחוֺת חֲצִי‎ see :52 (ᵐ5‎ Μωναιω, A Αμμανιθ).

מני.def:
H4508. Minni

I. מִנִּי‎ proper name, of a territory region of Armenia; — Jer 51:27 (|| אַשְׁכְּנַז אֲרָרָט,‎); = Assyrian Mannai Schr.COT on the passage; KGF 174.212.520

מנין.def:
H4510. minyan

מִנְרָן‎ noun [masculine] number; — construct ׳מ‎ Ezra 6:17.

מנית.def:
H4511. Minnith

מִנִּית‎ proper name, of a location in Ammonite territory, site unknown (4 Roman miles from Heshbon Euseb.Onom. 253, 33; compare BuhlGeogr. 266); — Judg 11:33 (ᵐ5‎ ἄχρις Ἀρνών, A εἰς Σεμωειθ, ᵐ5‎L Σεμενειθ); מ ׳חִטֵּי‎ Ezek 27:17 wheat of Minnîth (compare wheat from Ammon 2Chr 27:5) so Berthol, but dubious; Co conjectures וּנְכאֹת חִטִּים‎ wheat and storax.

[מְנֻסָה‎] see מְנוּסָה‎ below נוס‎.

מנלם.def:
H4512. minleh

[מִנְלֶה‎] noun [masculine] ? gain acquisition ? — Only suffix מִנְלָם לָאָרֶץ יִטֶּה לֹא‎ Job 15:29 (si vera lectio) their acquisition, but very dubious; Di (formerly) שִׁבֳּלִים‎, Hi מְלִלִים‎ ears, compare Bu; other conjectures see in Di; Du thinks hopelessly corrupt. — ᵐ5‎ σκιάν [i.e. צִלָּם‎], ᵑ6‎ their word [מִלָּתָם‎].

מנע.def:
H4513. mana

מָנַע‎ verb withhold, hold back (Late Hebrew id.; Zinjirli מנע‎ DHMSendsch. 60; Arabic ; Sabean מנע‎ Levy-OsZMG xix. 1865, 268; Aramaic מְנַע‎) —

Qal Perfect ׳מ‎ Gen 30:2; suffix מְנָעַ֫נִי‎ 1Sam 25:34; מָנַ֫עְתָּ‎ Psa 21:3; Neh 9:20, etc.; Imperfect יִמְנַעֿ‎ Psa 84:12; suffix יִמְנָעֵָ֫נִי‎ 2Sam 13:13 etc.; Imperative מְנַע‎ Prov 1:15; מִנְעִי‎ Jer 2:25; 31:16; Participle מֹנֵעַ‎ Prov 11:26; Jer 48:10; — withhold, followed by מִן‎ Gen 30:2 (object מְּרִיבֶֿטֶן‎), Amos 4:7 (rain), Neh 9:20 (manna; all subject ׳י‎); Job 22:7 (bread), 1Kin 20:7 (object omitted; both human subject), so Jer 48:10 (sword), Eccl 2:10 (heart), Jer 5:25 (good), Prov 3:27 (id., 1:15 (foot); Jer 2:25 (id.) 31:16 (voice); further, 2Sam 13:13 (woman), Jer 42:4 (knowledge), Job 31:16 (poor), Prov 23:13 (correction), object omitted ׳י‎ subject 30:7; מִן‎ omitted 11:26 (object corn); compare Psa 21:3 subject ׳י‎ (object שְׂפָתָיו אֲרֶשֶׁת‎ || לֵב תַּאֲוַת נָתַן‎), Job 20:13 figurative (wickedness), Ezek 31:15 ׳י‎ subject (object rivers); object person ׳י‎ subject followed by מן‎ Num 24:11; followed by מִן‎ + infinitive 1Sam 25:26, 34; followed by לְ‎, subject ׳י‎ Psa 84:12 (good).

Niph`al Perfect נִמְנַע‎ Joel 1:13; Imperfect יִמָּנַע‎ Job 38:15, etc.; be withholden followed by מִן‎, subject מִנְחָה‎ etc. Joel 1:13; light from wicked Job 38:15; Num 22:16 (followed by מִן‎ + infinitive); subject showers (רְבִבִים‎) Jer 3:3.

מנעול.def:
H4514. manul

מַנְעוּל‎ noun [masculine] bolt; — absolute הַמּ ׳כַּמּוֺת‎ Song 5:5 (of house-door); plural suffix מַנְעוּלָיו‎ Neh 3:3, מַנְעֻלָיו‎ 3:6; 3:13; 3:14; 3:15, all of city- gates, in phrase וּבְרִיחָיו (וּ)מַנ ׳דַּלְתֹתָיו‎.

מנעל.def:
H4515. minal

[מִנְעָל‎] noun masculine id., only suffix מִנְעָלֶ֑ךָ וּנְחשֶׁת בַּרְזֶל‎ Deut 33:25 (song).

מנעמים.def:
H4516. manammim

[מַנְעַמִּים‎] noun [masculine] plural delicacies, dainities; — only suffix בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶם וּבַלאֶֿלְחַם‎ Psa 141:4.

II. נעם‎ (perhaps to be assumed as √ of following, NeMarg. 10; Arabic speak in a low, Gentle voice, note, melody; Syriac rugivit, gentle sound, note; Late Hebrew נְלִימָה‎ melody; Ecclus 45:9 נעימה לתת‎ to make music; compare Hiph`il Ecclesiasticus 47:9b margin).

מנענעים.def:
H4517. menaanea

[מְנַעֲנֵעַ‎] noun [masculine] apparently a kind of rattle, only וּבִמְנַָֽעַנְעִים‎ 2Sam 6:5, in list of musical instruments; ᵐ5‎ κύμβαλα, but this usually (12 t.) = מְצִלְתַּיִם‎; ᵑ9‎ sisitra; the sistrum (Gr. σεῖστρον, from σείω) was much used in Egypt; it was a small metal frame with loose metal bars carrying loose rings, borne and swung or shaken in the hand, see WilkinsonAnc. Kgyptians (1878), i. 497 ff. NowArchaeology l. 273 BenzArchaeology 278 WePsalms Eng. Trans. p. 233.

נוֺעַדְיָה‎ see יעד‎.

מנקית.def:
H4518. menaqqith

[מְנַקִּיָּה‎] noun masculine sacrificial bowl; — plural מְנַקִיּוֺת‎ Jer 52:19; מְנַקִּיֹּת‎ Num 4:7; suffix מְנַקִּיֹּתָיו‎ Exod 25:29; 37:16.

נקט‎ see קוט‎.

מנשה.def:
H4519. Menashsheh

מְנַשֶּׁה‎136 proper name, masculine person and tribe Manasseh (interpretation of Gen 41:51 as Pi`el causative √II. נשׁה‎ q. v.); — ׳מ‎ 46:20 +; מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה‎ 41:51 + (on Judg 18:30 see משֶׁה‎); with article (strangely), ׳הַמְֿ‎ Josh 1:12 10t. (see below); ᵐ5‎ Μαν(ν)ασση; —

1

a. Manasseh, eldest son of Joseph Gen 41:51; 48:1, 13, 14 (twice in verse); 48:17, 20 (twice in verse), also 50:23 (father of Machir; all E), 46:20; 48:5 (both P).

b. of tribe, often + Ephraim (see אֶפְרַיִם‎): (I) the part west of Jordan: a. מ ׳בְּנֵי‎ Josh 16:9; 17:2a (הַנּוֺתָרִים ׳בנימֿ‎), 17:2 b; 17:6; 17:12 (all J E), 1Chr 7:29; 9:3 (וּמ אֶפְרַיִם ׳בְּנֵי‎; Josh 13:29 see below); β. ׳מ‎ alone, 17:5, 8 (twice in verse); 17:9b; 17:11, 17; Deut 34:2 (וּמ אֶפְרַיִם ׳אֶרֶץ‎; all J E), 2Chr 30:10 (id.), Josh 16:4; 17:7; 17:9a; 17:10 (all P), also apparently Deut 33:17 (poem), Judg 1:27; 6:15, 35; 7:23; Isa 9:20 (twice in verse); Psa 80:3 10t. Chronicles; γ. מ ׳מַטֵּה‎ 1Chr 6:55; מ מַטֵּה ׳חֲצִי‎ Josh 21:6, 25; 1Chr 12:32 (van d. H v.12:31); מ חֲצִי מַטֵּה ׳מַחֲצִית‎ 6:46 (but on text see Kit); מ מַטּוֺת ׳שְׁנֵי וְאֶפְרַיִם‎ Josh 14:4 (P); δ. מ שֵׁבֶט ׳חֲצִי‎ 1Chr 27:20; with article הַמְֿ ׳הַשֵּׁבֶט‎ Josh 13:7 (D). (2) of Manasseh east of Jordan; α. מ ׳בְּנֵי‎ 22:30-31, (P); β. ׳מ‎ alone, Judg 11:29 (distinctly of territory), 12:4 (but on text see GFM), Psa 60:9 = 108:9; הַמ ׳חֲצִי‎ 1Chr 27:21; γ. מ ׳מַטֵּה‎ Josh 17:1a 20:8 (both P), 1Chr 6:47; מ מַטֵּה ׳חֲצִי‎ Josh 22:1 (D), Num 34:14; Josh 21:5, 27 (all P), 1Chr 6:56; מ ׳בְּנֵי מַטֵּה חֲצִי‎ Josh 13:29 (P); δ. מ שֵׁבֶט ׳חֲצִי‎ Deut 3:13 (D), Josh 13:29; 22:13, 15 (all P), 1Chr 15:18, 23, 26; 12:38 (van d. H v.12:37); מ שֵׁבֶט ׳חֲצִי בֶּןיֿוֺסֵף‎ Num 32:33 (P); with article הַמְֿ שֵׁבֶט ׳חֲצִי‎ Josh 1:12; 4:12; 12:6; 18:7; 22:1, 7 (all D), 22:9-10, 11, 21 (all P). Here belong also (chiefly) references to ׳מ‎ as father of Machir (compare Gen 50:23 above): Num 27:1; 32:39-40, 36:1; Josh 13:31; 17:1, 3(all P), 1Chr 7:14, 17; and of Jair Deut 3:14 (D), Num 32:41 (P), 1Kin 4:13 (compare יָאִיר מָכִיר,‎). (3) of undivided tribe (never מ ׳שֵׁבֶט‎): α. מ ׳בְּנֵי‎ Num 1:34; 2:20; 7:54; 26:29; 36:12 (all P); β. ׳מ‎ alone, 1:10; 26:28, 34; 27:1b (all P), Ezek 48:4-5, γ. מ ׳מַטֵּה‎ Num 1:35; 2:20; 13:11, מ בְּנֵי ׳מַטֵּה‎ 10:23; 34:13 (all P).

2 son of Hezekiah, and king of Judah (Assyrian Menasê, Minsê SchrCOT 2Kin 21:1); — 20:21; 21:1 9t. Kings, 12 t. Chronicles, Jer 15:4.

3 two who had taken strange wives:

a. Ezra 10:30.

b. Ezra 10:33.

מנשי.def:
H4520. Menashshi

מְנַשִּׁי‎ adjective, of a people of ׳מ‎ 1; only with article ׳הַמְֿ‎, as collective noun, of tribe east of Jordan: Deut 4:43; 2Kin 10:33; הַמְֿ ׳שֵׁבֶט‎ Deut 29:7; 1Chr 26:32.

מְנָת‎ see מנה‎

מנת.def:
H4490. manah

מָנָה‎ noun feminine part, portion; — ׳מ‎ Exod 29:26 4t.; (on מְנָָֽתֿ‎ Jer 13:25, compare Psa 16:5, see מְנָת‎); plural מָנוֺת‎ 1Sam 1:4-5t.; suffix מָֽנוֺתֶ֫הָ‎ Est 2:9; — part, portion, especially choice portion, Exod 29:26; Lev 7:33; 8:29 (all of sacrificial animal; all P); compare 2Chr 31:19; also 1Sam 1:4-5, of distributive of choice bits Neh 8:10, 12; Est 9:19, 22; compare also 2:9 (see Dan 1:5, 10).

מס.def:
H4523. mas

II. [מַס‎] adjective despairing (literally melting, i.e. failing, collapsing); — לַמָּס‎ Job 6:14 to him also despaireth belongeth kindness, etc.

מסב.def:
H4524. mesab

or mesibbim or mesibboth מֵסַב‎ noun [masculine] that which surrounds, or is round; —

1. a. plural surrounding places, ׳יְרוּשׁ מְסִבֵּי‎ 2Kin 23:5 places round about Jerusalem.

b. as adverb מֵסַב‎ round about 1Kin 6:29; feminine plural מְסִבּוֺת‎ on all sides, in all directions, Job 37:12 (of cloud Di < of lightning Bu Du).

2 suffix מְסִבּוֺ‎ Song 1:12 dubious: round table Ew De; cushion, divan Bae Kau; compare on all these Bu. — מְסִבָּ֑י‎ Psa 140:10 see סבב‎

Hiph`il

מסבה.def:
H4524. mesab

or mesibbim or mesibboth מֵסַב‎ noun [masculine] that which surrounds, or is round; —

1. a. plural surrounding places, ׳יְרוּשׁ מְסִבֵּי‎ 2Kin 23:5 places round about Jerusalem.

b. as adverb מֵסַב‎ round about 1Kin 6:29; feminine plural מְסִבּוֺת‎ on all sides, in all directions, Job 37:12 (of cloud Di < of lightning Bu Du).

2 suffix מְסִבּוֺ‎ Song 1:12 dubious: round table Ew De; cushion, divan Bae Kau; compare on all these Bu. — מְסִבָּ֑י‎ Psa 140:10 see סבב‎

Hiph`il

מסגר.def:
H4525. masger

מַסְגֵּר‎ noun [masculine]

1 locksmith, smith.

2 dungeon: — always absolute:

1 collective smiths, ׳וְהַמּ וְכָלהֶֿחָרָשׁ‎ 2Kin 24:14 compare 24:16, Jer 24:1; 29:2.

2 dungeon Isa 24:22 (compare סגר‎ Pu`al); figurative of exile 42:7 (מִמּ ׳הוֺצִיא‎); מִמּ ׳הוֺצִיאָה נַפְשִׁי‎ Psalm 142:8.

מסגרת.def:
H4526. misgereth

מִסְגֶּ֫רֶת‎ noun feminine 1. border, rim.

2 fastness; — absolute ׳מ‎ Exod 25:27; 37:14; construct ׳מ‎ 25:25; 37:12; suffix מִסְגַּרְתּוֺ‎ 25:25; 37:12; plural absolute מִסְגְּרוֺת‎ 1Kin 7:28 +; suffix מִסְגְּרֹתֶיהָ‎ 7:35; 7:36, etc.; —

1 border, rim (enclosure), of sacred table in tabernacle Exod 25:25 (twice in verse); 25:27 = 37:12 (twice in verse); 37:14; of bases of the sea, in temple 1Kin 7:28 (twice in verse); 7:29, 31, 32, 35, 36 (compare Benz), also 2Kin 16:17.

2 fastness, מִמּ ׳וְיַחְרְגוּ‎ Psa 18:46 = 2Sam 22:46 (see חרג‎) and they shall come quaking out of their fastnesses, so Micah 7:17 (יִרְגְּזוּ‎, like reptiles), all of nations, in awe of ׳י‎.

II. סגר‎ (√ of following; compare apparently Arabic fill with water Lane1308, torrent that fills everything Idib.; Syriac imber vehemens, and Samaritan אַסְגָּר‎, compare GeiNachgel. Schr. iv. 186).

מסד.def:
H4527. massad

מַסַּד‎ noun [masculine] foundation; — מִמַּסַּד‎ 1Kin 7:9 || עַדהַֿטְּפָחוֺת‎; Co reads מַסַּד‎ also Ezek 41:8 (for מיּ֯סְדוֺת ᵑ0‎).

מסדרון.def:
H4528. misderon

[מִסְדְּרוֺן‎] noun [masculine] porch, colonnade ? (place of a row (of pillars) ?); — only with, ה‎ locative: הַמִּסְדְּר֑וֺנָה אֵהוּד וַיֵּצֵא‎ Judg 3:23 precise meaning dubious, compare GFM.

סהר‎ (√ of following = be round?; compare Late Hebrew סַ֫הַר‎ a round place; Assyrian sîru, enclosing wall; also Phoenician סהרו‎

proper name, of a location).

מסה.def:
H4529. masah

[מָסָה‎] verb melt, dissolve, be liquefied (Ethiopic liquefy; Aramaic מְסָא‎ melt away, dissolve, decay, coagulate; Assyrian masû is wash; see also מסס‎); — only

Hiph`il Perfect3plural הִמְסִיו‎ Josh 14:8 (on form see Ges§ 75 R.17). Imperfect sf . יַּעמסֵם‎ Psa 147:18; 2masculine singular וַתֶּ֫מֶס‎ 39:12; אַמְסֶה‎ 6:7; — cause to dissolve, melt, ice 147:18; hyperb. אַמְּסֶה עַרְשִׁי בְּדִמְעָתִי‎ 6:7 with my tears I cause my bed to dissolve; חֲמוּדוֺ כָּעָשׁ וַתֶּמֶס‎ 39:12 = consume, cause to vanish; figurative followed by לֵב‎ = intimidate Josh 14:8.

I. [מַסָּה‎] see מסס‎. II, III. מַסָּה‎ see נסה‎.

[מִסָּה‎] see מִסַּת‎. מַסְוֶה‎ see סוה‎

מְסוּכָה‎ = מְשׂוּכָה‎ see II. סוך‎ (שׂוך‎).

מסוה.def:
H4533. masveh

מַסְוֶה‎ noun [masculine] veil; — absolute ׳מ עַלמָּֿנָיו‎ Exod 34:33 compare 34:34; 34:35 (P).

מסוכה.def:
H4534. mesukah

מְסוּכָה‎ noun feminine hedge (|| form of מְשֻׂכָה‎ q. v. below שׂוך‎); — only in figure מִמְּסוּכָה יָשָׁר‎ Micah 7:4, read מְס ׳יְשָׁרָם‎ (|| כְּחֵדֶק טוֺבָם‎), their most upright one is a hedge (an obstruction).

מסח.def:
H4535. massach

מַסָּח‎ dubious word, only in מַסָּ֑ח הַבַּיִת אֶתמִֿשְׁמֶרֶת וּשְׂמַרְתֶּם‎ 2Kin 11:6; Thes and others below v נסח‎ = for plucking away i.e. repulse, defence, but very uncertain; probably textual error; omitted by ᵐ5‎B We Stap. 354; ᵐ5‎L Μεσσαε.

[מִסְחָר‎] see סחר‎

מסחר.def:
H4536. mischar

[מִסְחָר‎] noun masculine apparently merchandise; — construct הָרֹכְלִים מִסְחַר‎ 1Kin 10:15, but text probably corrupt; Klo proposes מִסַּחַר‎, so BuhlLex 13; || 2Chr 9:14 has הַסֹּחֲרִים‎, and so Benz here (for both words of MT).

מסך.def:
H4537. masak

מָסַךְ‎ verb mix, produce by mixing (compare perhaps מֶזֶג מזג,‎ BaES 33, 51); —

Qal Perfect3masculine singular ׳מ‎ Isa 19:14; מָֽסְכָה‎ Prov 9:2; מָסָ֑כְתִּי‎ 9:5; Psa 102:10; Infinitive construct מְסֹךְ‎ Isa 5:22; —

1 pour, only figurative, עִוְעִים רוּחַ ׳מ בְּקִרְבָּהּ‎ Isa 19:14 (subject ׳מ‎); mix, with accusative שֵׁכָר‎ 5:22; i.e. make a choice drink by mixing with spices, etc. (mixing with water came later, compare 2Macc 15:39) Löwp. 419 Frä162f, 171 f. NowArchaeology 1, 120 BenzArchaeology 95; object יַיִן‎ figurative, subject wisdom Prov 9:2, 5; מָסָ֑כְתִּי בִּבְכִי שִׁקֻּוַי‎ Psa 102:10 my drink with weeping have I mixed (see Assyrian [akâl] ul âkul, bikîtum kurmati, mê ul aštî, dîmtu maštîtî ZimBP 34).

מסכה.def:
H4540. mesukkah

[מְסֻכָֿה‎] noun feminine that with which one is covered, covering; — suffix מְסֻכָֿתָ֑ךָ‎ Ezek 28:13 (so Baer Ginsb; van d. H. ׳מְסֻכּ‎) all precious stones were thy covering (= thou wast covered with them); — the tradition is strong in favour of Raph¢, but sense favours derivation from סכך‎.

מסכן.def:
H4542. misken

מִסְכֵּן‎ adjective poor, only Ecclesiastes (Late Hebrew id.; Aramaic id.; PS2632; Arabic ; Ethiopic Di382; √ dubious; usually derived from III. סכן‎ q. v.; perhaps loan-word; according to JenZA iv (1889), 271 f Zimib. vii (1892), 353 = Assyrian muškênu, beggar, needy one); — always absolute ׳מ‎: — מ ׳יֶלֶד וְחָכָם‎ Eccl 4:13 (opposed to וּכְסִיל זֶקֵן מֶלֶח‎); מ ׳אִישׁ חָכָם‎ 9:15, הַמּ ׳הָאִישׁ‎ 9:15; as substantive ׳הַמּ‎ 9:16 the poor man.

מסכנות.def:
H4543. miskenoth

מִסְכְּנוֺת‎ noun feminine plural supply, storage (DlProv 186); — עָרֵי ׳(חַ)מ‎ Exod 1:11 (J), 1Kin 9:19 2Chr 8:6, 4; 17:12; ׳מ ׳ע‎16:4 probably corrupt (Be and others; see עִיר‎); ׳מ‎ alone 32:28 storage-places, magazines.

מסכנת.def:
H4544. miskenuth

מִסְכֵּנֻת‎ noun feminine poverty, scarcity, Deut 8:9.

מִסְכְּנוֺת‎ see I. סכן‎.

מַסְלוּל מְסִלָּה,‎ see סלל‎.

[מִסְמֵר‎], מַסְמְרִים‎ etc. see סמר‎ (שׂמר‎).

מסכת.def:
H4545. masseketh

מספר.def:

1. a. number, Judg 7:6 the number of those lapping, ׳מִס לַכּוֺכָבִים‎ Psa 147:4, + often (37 t. PH); וגו דִּבְרֵי בְּמִסְמַּר הַמִּסְמָּר עָלָה ׳לֹא‎ 1Chr 27:24 (read בְּסֵפֶר‎) the number did not come up into (was not recorded in) the book of the daily doings, etc.; redundant after number, 2Sam 21:20 twenty-four (in) number; מ ׳אֵין‎ it was (they were) innumerable Gen 41:49 (E), with לְ‎ Judg 6:5; 7:12; 1Chr 22:16; 2Chr 12:3, מ אֵין ׳לִתְבוּנָתוֺ‎ Psa 147:5 (of ׳י‎); absolute Jer 2:32; Job 21:33; Song 6:8; מ ׳עַדאֵֿין‎ = id. Job 5:9; 9:10; Psa 40:13, מ לָהֶם ׳וְאֵין‎ Jer 46:23; מ ׳לְאֵין‎ 1Chr 22:4; מ ׳וְאֵין‎ Psa 104:25; 105:34; Joel 1:6; מ ׳הֲיֵשׁ לִגְדוּדָיו‎ Job 25:3 can his bands be numbered ? without אֵין‎ = numerable, i.e. few, מ מְתָיו ׳וִיהִי‎ Deut 33:6 but let his men be few מ ׳יָמִים‎ Num 9:20, ׳מ‎ alone Isa 10:19, usually in combination, מ ׳מְתֵי‎ = a few men Gen 34:30 (J), Deut 4:27; Jer 44:28; 1Chr 16:19; Psa 105:12, מ ׳אַנְשֵׁי‎ Ezek 12:16; so מ ׳שְׁנוֺת‎ Job 16:22; adverb phrase חַיֵּיהֶם יְמֵי מִסְפַר‎ Eccl 2:3 = during all their lives, compare 5:17; Ecclesiastes 6:18 = appointed (normal) number, ׳מ מֲַלֵּא יָמֶיךָ‎ Exod 23:26 (E).

b. with preposition בְּמ ׳מְעַט ׃בְּ‎ Ezek 5:3 few in number; ׳בְּמ‎ by (exact) count, tale 2Sam 2:15; Deut 25:2; 1Chr 9:28 (twice in verse), so probably Ezek 20:37 read ᵐ5 בְּמִסְמַּר‎ Toy for מָסֹרֶת ᵑ0‎; in (prescribed) number Num 29:18 6t. Numbers 29 (P), Ezra 3:4; = acc. to (proportioned to) the number of Lev 25:15. 15 + often; ׳לְמִס‎ according to number Judg 21:23; Josh 4:5, 8 (JE) Num 14:29 (P) Ezek 4:5; 1Chr 27:1; ׳כְּמִס‎ = id. 1Kin 18:31; Num 15:12 (twice in verse) (P); so ׳מ‎ alone (adverb accusative) Exod 16:16 (P) Job 1:5; Jer 2:28; 11:13. — Num 23:10b read מִי סָפַר‎, compare va, so ᵐ5‎ Di SoKau.

2 recounting, relation הַחֲלוֺם מִסְמַּר‎ Judg 7:15 the recounting of the dream.

מעזיה.def:
ו‎

ו‎, Waw, sixth letter; in modern Hebrew = numeral 6; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

וָ וּ, וְ,‎

demonstrative adverb and

conjunction so, then, and (Phoenician, Moabite, Aramaic ו‎; Arabic ; Ethiopic Assyrian u DlW (but between verbs the usually connective is the enclitic ma KAT2. 508, Dl§§ 82, 150). The use in Hebrew shews that original וְ‎ was not a merely copulative conjunction, but that it possessed a demonstrative force (compare Dr§ 122), which is often perceptible as such, though in other cases, from its being applied to denote mere juxtaposition or connection [compare Greek τε, and Latin tum .... tum = 'both .... and,' both properly demonstratives: Assyrian ma has also a demonstrative force, Dl§ 79], it is less palpable) — וְ‎ before shwa' mobile or a labial is vocalized וּ‎; often before a tone-syll., when the word itself has a disj. accent, וָ‎ (as וַָמתִּי׃‎ Gen 19:19; וָמֵ֖תוּ‎ 33:13; וָמֵ֑ת‎ 44:9; וָחָֽיָה׃‎ Exod 1:16; וָיָ֑מָּה‎ Josh 15:46; וָ֔לֹ֕א‎ 2Sam 13:26; וָאָ֖רֶץ‎ Isa 26:19; וָקָ֔מוּ‎ 49:7; וָחָֽתָּה׃‎ Jer 48:1; וָרָֹע‎ Psa 10:15); especially when it forms with the preceding word a pair, whether of parallel or opposed ideas (as וָכֹה כֹּה‎ Exod 2:12, וָמִ֖י מִי‎ 10:8, וָאָ֑בֶן אֶבֶן‎ Deut 25:13; וָדֹ֑ר דֹּר‎ 32:7 +; וָבֹ֔הוּ תֹּהוּ‎ Gen 1:2, וָרֶמֶ֛שׂ בְּהֵמָה‎ 1:24, וָרָֽע׃ טוֺב‎ 2:19, וָנָ֖ד נָע‎ 4:12, וָלָ֖יְלָה וְיוֺם וָחֹ֛רֶף וְקַיִץ‎ 8:22, וֵָלךְ׃ קַח‎ 12:19, וָאָֽרֶץ׃ שָׁמַיִם‎ 14:19, וָאָ֑תָּה אֲנִי‎ 31:44, וָה֑וּא אֲנִי‎ 41:11, וָשׁוּבוּ עִבְרוּ‎ Exod 32:27, וָהֵ֛ם אַתָּה‎ Num 16:16, וָמֶ֑לָךְ אֱלֹהִים‎ 1Kin 21:13, וָנֶ֖כֶד נִין‎ Isa 14:22, וָשֶׁ֖בֶר שֹׁד‎ 59:7; and often: see more fully Bö§ 600); occasionally also with a conjunctive accent (as לְעֹלָֽם׃ וָשַחי‎ Gen 3:22 compare Lev 18:5, שָׁם וָמַ֣תְנוּ‎ 2Kin 7:4, חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וָאָ֣רֶץ‎ Isa 65:17; Prov 25:3, גָּדוֺל׃ וָשֶשׁבֶר שֹׁ֖ד‎ Jer 48:3, compare 32:29). — וְ‎ is used very freely and widely in Hebrew, but also with much delicacy, to express relations and shades of meaning which Western languages would usually indicate by distinct particles. But in Hebrew particles such as לָכֵן לְמַעַן, בַּעֲבוּר, אוּלָם, אָכֵן, אַךְ, אָז, אוֺ,‎, etc., were reserved for cases in which special emphasis or distinctness was desired: their frequent use was felt instinctively to be inconsistent with the lightness and grace of movement which the Hebrew ear loved; and thus in AV, RV, words like or, then, but, notwithstanding, howbeit, so, thus, therefore, that, constantly appear, where the Hebrew has simply וְ‎.

1 And, connecting both words (see above), and sentences (Gen 1:5 וג קָרָא ׳וְלַחשֶׁךְ‎). When three, four, or more words follow, the conjunction may connect them all, as 7:21; 10:2 (6 t.) 24:35 (7 t.) Josh 7:24 (10 t.) 2Sam 17:28f.: often however it is prefixed only to the last, as Gen 5:32; 10:1; Deut 18:10 etc.; occas. even it connects only the first two, 1Kin 8:47; Isa 1:13; Psa 45:9; Job 42:9. Remarkably, however, וְ‎ as a mere conjunction is, as a rule, not in classical Hebrew attached directly to verbs (especially in the perfect), the construction with וְ‎ consecutive (see

2) being (as in Moabite) preferred: thus וַיִּבֶן יָצָא‎ is said, not וּבָנָה יָצָא‎. Exceptions in classical Hebrew are (a) sometimes where synonyms are coupled, as Num 23:19 וְדִבֶּר ֗֗֗ אָמַר‎, Deut 2:30; Judg 5:26; 1Sam 12:2; Isa 1:2 ורוממתי גדּלתי‎ 2:11; 5:14; 8:8; 19:6; 29:20; (b) isolated cases, difficult to reduce to rule (perhaps sometimes due to textual error), as Gen 28:6; 38:5; Judg 3:23; 7:13; 16:18; 1Sam 1:12; 3:13; 4:19; 5:7; 10:9; 17:38, 48; 25:20 and elsewhere (in other passages, apparently similar, the perfect and וְ‎ has a frequent. force (see 2), as Gen 37:3; Exod 36:29f.; Num 10:17f. 21:15, 20; 1Sam 2:22; 16:14; 17:34f. (see Dr) 27:9; 2Sam 16:13; 17:17, perhaps also Gen 15:6; 21:25; 34:5). In later parts of OT, probably through Aramaic influence, the perfect with simple וְ‎ occurs more frequently: so especially in Ecclesiastes, where it is all but universal (e.g. 2:11-12, 13, 15 etc.). With the imperfect, the simple וְ‎ is not so unidiomatic, even in classical Hebrew (compare 3); see 1:9, 26; 9:27; 17:2; 22:17; 27:29; Exod 23:8 (frequently) 24:7; Num 14:12; Deut 17:13; 30:12-13, Josh 3:13; 7:3; Judg 7:3; 13:8; Isa 5:29; 14:10; often also in Jeremiah, Isa2, Job, Psalms, e.g. 40:30; 41:20 (Dr§ 116: contrast 28:13). See more fully Dr§ 130-4 Ges§ 112. 6. Special senses: —

a. it sometimes = and specially, Gen 3:16; 1Kin 11:1 many strange women, and specially the daughter of Pharaoh, Isa 1:1 Judah and (= and particularly) Jerusalem, 2:1; 9:7; Psa 18:1.

b. and in particular ('und zwar'), and that (explicative), Gen 4:4; Judg 7:22; 1Sam 17:40 וּבַיַּלְקוּט‎, 28:3 in Ramah, and that in his city (unusual: text suspicious), 2Sam 13:20 וְשֹׁמֵמָה‎ and that desolate, Isa 57:11 I have been silent וּמֵעוֺלָם‎ and that from of old, 32:7; Jer 15:13; Amos 3:11 (si vera lectio), 4:10; Zech 9:9b Mal 1:11; Psa 68:10; Prov 3:12; Lam 3:26; Eccl 8:2; Dan 1:3; 8:10; 9:25, 27; Neh 8:13; 1Chr 9:27; 2Chr 8:13; 29:27 (but' even' for ו‎, before ל‎ and infinitive, e.g. in Isa 44:28; Jer 17:10; 19:12, is wrong; see Ew§ 351 c, Dr§ 206).

c. sometimes it introduces an idea which so exceeds or adds to what has preceded, that it is nearly equivalent to also, 1Sam 25:43; 1Kin 2:22 ask also the kingdom for him; unusually Hosea 8:6 והוא מישׂראל כי‎ for of Israel is it also, Eccl 5:6 והבלים‎ (see De) 2Chr 27:5 (but see ᵐ5‎). Or it may be rendered yea: so especially in the ascending numerations 3-4 Amos 1:3, 6, 9, 11, 13; 2:1, 4, 6; Prov 30:18, 21, 29, 6-7 6:16; Job 5:19, 7-8 Micah 5:4 — the first number being aggravated, or augmented, by a higher. In one idiom וּגְבוּל‎, occurring in geographic descriptions, it is used peculiarly, seemingly = at the same time: Num 34:6 and as for the western border, וּגְבוּל הַגָּדוֺל הַיָּם לָכֶם וְהָיָה‎ the great sea shall be to you also (German 'zugleich') a border, Deut 3:16 וּגְבוּל הַנַּחַל תּוֺךְ‎ the middle of the stream being at the same time the border, 3:17; Josh 13:23, 27; 15:12, 47 (but these, except Num 34:6, might be cases of 5c γ).

d. it connects alternative cases, so that it = or: Exod 20:10, 17; 21:16 he that stealeth a man בְיָדוֺ וְנִמְצָא וּמְכָרוֺ‎ and selleth him, and (= or if) he be found in his hand, 21:17; Lev 21:14; 22:23-24, Prov 29:9 (Fl Ew RV: whether . . . or) Job 31:13, 16, 26, etc.

e. it connects contrasted ideas, where in our idiom the contrast would be expressed explicitly by but; in such cases prominence is usually given to the contrasted idea by its being placed immediately after the conjunction: Gen 2:17 but of the tree of the knowledge . . . thou shalt not eat, 4:2, 5; 6:8; 17:21; 31:10 etc., 1Kin 2:26; 10:7; 11:32, 34; 15:14; Prov 10:1-2, 3, 4 + often; even after לֹא‎ (where כִּי‎ or אִם כִּי‎ might be expected), as Gen 42:10; Exod 21:18; Lev 26:45; Deut 11:11; Judg 19:12; 1Kin 3:11.

f. it introduces a contrasted idea in such a way as to suggest a question, especially before a pronoun, Judg 14:16 I told it not to my father or my mother, אַגִּיד וְלָךְ‎ and shall I told it unto thee? 2Sam 11:11; Jer 25:29 תִנָּקוּ הִנָּקֵה וְאַתֶּם‎ and shall ye be guiltless? 45:5; Ezek 20:31; 33:25b Jonah 4:11. So the וְ‎ consecutive and perfect (see 2a), Exod 5:5 וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּם‎ and will ye make them rest from their burdens? Num 16:10 וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם‎ and seek ye the priesthood also? 1Sam 25:11; Isa 66:9; Psa 50:21 and shall I keep silence? Job 32:16 (compare Dr§ 119 γ).

g. attaching a fresh subj. (or object) to a clause already grammatically complete, it = and also, Gen 2:9b Num 16:2, 18 and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, ואהרן ומשׁה‎ and Moses and Aaron (stood also), 16:27; Exod 35:22; Judg 6:5; Gen 1:16; b 12:17; 44:2; 46:15; Exod 29:3; Jer 32:29 (compare DrSm. i. 6, 11, & p. 293): when the idea thus attached is subordinate, or not logically embraced in the principal predicate, it approximates to the Arabic or 'waw of association' (followed by an accusative: WAG ii. § 37), Est 4:16 אָצוּם וְנַעֲרֹתַי אֲנִי‎ I will fast (singular) and (= with) my maidens, Exod 21:4; 1Sam 25:42; 29:10b (but insert here אַתָּה‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Sam 12:30 (but read וּבָהּ‎, as 1Chr 20:2) 1Sam 20:10; Neh 6:12; Gen 4:20; Isa 42:5; Jer 19:1 (but read מזקני וְלָקַחְתָּ֫‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Chr 2:3; 13:11; compare Jer 22:7 (וְכֵלָיו אִישׁ‎), Job 41:12. Whether Isa 48:16 וְרוּחוֺ‎ belongs here, is dubious

h. וְ‎ repeated = both . . . and (but גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎) is more usual in this sense); Gen 34:28; Num 9:14; Josh 9:23; 2Sam 5:8 (text dubious), Isa 16:5; 38:15; Jer 13:14; 21:6; 32:14 (text dubious) 32:20; 40:8; Psa 76:7; Job 34:29; Dan 8:13; Neh 12:28.

i. a repetition of the same word with וְ‎ interposed expresses (a) diversity (rare), Deut 25:13 וָאֶבֶן אֶבֶן‎ a weight and a weight, i.e. different weights (explained by וּקְטַנָּה גְּדֹלָה‎), 25:14; Prov 20:23; Psa 12:3 וָלֵב בְּלֵב‎ with a heart and a heart = with a double heart, 1Chr 12:33 וָלֵב לֵב בְּלֹא‎; (b) distribution (except in וָדֹר דֹּר‎ Deut 32:7; Isa 13:20 +?Intr. 505) Psa 87:5; 1Chr 26:13 וָשָֽׁעַר׃ לְשַׁעַר‎ = for every gate, 28:14 (twice in verse); 2Chr 8:14; 34:13; 35:15; Ezra 10:14 וָעִיר עִיר זִקְנֵי‎ elders of every city, Neh 13:24; Est 1:8, 22 (twice in verse); 2:12; 3:4, 12 (4 t. in verse); 8:9 (twice in verse); strengthened by כָּלֿ‎2Chr 11:12 ועיר עיר בכל‎ in every several city, 19:5; 28:25; 31:19; 32:28; Est 2:11 ויום בכליֿום‎, 3:14; 4:3; 8:11, 13, 17 (twice in verse); 9:21, 27, 28; Psalm 45:18; Psa 145:13 (common in post-Biblical Hebrew, especially with כל‎).

j. it is used in the formulation of proverbs (the Vav adaequationis, הִשְׁתַּוָּאָה וָו‎) as Prov 17:3; 25:3, 20, 25 cold waters to a thirsty soul and good news from a far country (i.e. they are like each other), 26:3, 9, 14, 20; 27:21; Eccl 5:2; 7:1; 8:8; compare 9:11; Psa 19:5; 125:2; Job 14:11f.; 14:19 (compare in Arabic 'every man and his cares [accusative],' 'every thing and its price,' i.e. they go together: 'merchants and dogs [accusative] of Seleucia,' i.e. they are like one another: see FlKl. Schr. iii. 535 f.). More rarely in the opposite order, 5:7; 12:11. But 1Sam 12:15b cannot be thus explained: read with וּבְמַלְכְּכֶם ᵐ5‎, and see Dr.

k. in circumstantial clauses וְ‎ introduces a statement of the concomitant conditions under which the action denoted by the principal verb takes place: in such cases, the relation expressed by וְ‎ must often in English be stated explicitly by a conjunction, as when, since, seeing, though, etc., as occasion may require. So very often, as Gen 11:4 let us build a tower בַשָּׁמַיִם וְראֹשׁוֺ‎ and its top in the heavens (= with its top in etc.), 18:12 shall I have pleasure, זָקֵן וַאדֹנִי‎ and my lord is old (= my lord being old)? Judg 16:15 How sayest thou, I love thee, אִתִּי אֵין וְלִבְּךָ‎ and (= when) thy heart is not with me? and especially with a person pronoun, Gen 15:2 what wilt thou give me עֲרִירִי הֹלֵךְ וְאָנֹכִי‎ and I (= the case being that I) am going hence childless? 18:13; 20:3 lo, thou wilt die because of the woman thou hast taken בָּֽעַל׃ בְּעֻלַת וְהִוא‎ = seeing she is married, 24:62 ישֵׁב וְהוּא‎ = since or for he was dwelling (different from וַיֵּשֶׁב‎ = and he proceeded to dwell), 26:27 וְאַתֶּם‎ seeing ye hate me, Judg 13:9 and came to her ישֶׁבֶת וְהִיא‎ = as she was sitting, 1Sam 18:23; 1Kin 19:19 +? Psa 72:12 the afflicted לוֺ וְאֵיןעֹֿזֵר‎ and (= when) he has no helper (compare Job 29:12), Job 104:25 מִסְמָּר וְאֵין‎, Job 105:34; 5:9. See more fully Dr§ 156-60 Ges§ 141, R 2. (The analogous use of the is very common in Arabic: Wii. § 183.) Introducing an appeal to a fact confirmatory of some statement or promise, it almost = as truly as (compare Ew§ 340 c) Hosea 12:6 and J. is God of hosts, J. is his name! Joel 4:20; Amos 9:5-6 Isa 51:15 and I [who promise this] am J. thy God, who . . . . ! Jer 29:23; Psa 89:38b (compare in Qoran the frequently 'And God is .. . . . [the mighty, the merciful, etc.]').

2 The ו‎ consecutive (formerly called the Waw 'conversive'); —

a. with the

imperfect (וַּ‎ with following daghesh; before וָ א,‎), as וַיּאֹמֶר‎ properly = and he proceeded to say, chiefly in contin. of a preceding perfect tense (so Moabite);

b. with the

perfect (וְ‎, — in 1 & 2 singular, the tone, with certain exceptions [see Dr§ 110], being thrown forward to the ultima), as וְיָָֽשַׁבְתָּ֫‎ properly so [namely, as limited by a verb, or other term, preceding] hadst thou sat, chiefly in continuation of a preceding imperfect tense, in its various senses of future, jussive, or frequentative. Thefurther analysis of these idioms belongs to the grammar; see on a DrCh. vi., Ges§ 111, and on

b DrCh. viii. Ges§ 112. Here it must suffice to note — (a) ו‎ consecutive (especially with the imperfect) frequently couples two verbs in such a manner that the first, indicating the general character of the action, receives its closer definition in the second: in such cases, the first may often be represented in English by an adverb, as Gen 26:18 וַיַּחְמֹּר וַיָּשָׁב‎ and he turned and dug = and he dug again; so often; and similarly with הוֺסִיף‎ 25:1, מִהַר‎ 24:18, הוֺאִיל‎ Josh 7:7, etc.; more exceptionally, Gen 30:27; Est 8:6, and (not consecutive) Gen 47:6; Job 23:3; Song 2:3; Lam 3:26 (see Ges§ 120, 2 a; compare in Syriac Nö§ 335-6. In Arabic the stronger form of the conjugation here corresponds: Wii. § 140). (b) וַּ ‎ with the imperfect sometimes expresses a contrast = and yet, Gen 32:31 I have seen God face to face וַתִּנָּצֵל‎ and yet my soul is delivered, Deut 4:33; 2Sam 3:8; 19:29; Isa 51:12; Psa 73:14; 144:3; Job 10:8 + (compare Dr§ 74 β). (c) there is a tendency in the later books of the OT to use the perfect with simple וְ‎, where the classical language would employ the imperfect with וַּ ‎ (compare above

1); so especially in Ecclesiastes, where וַּ ‎ occurs thrice only, Job 1:17; 4:1, 7. (d) a double perfect with ו‎ consecutive is sometimes used, informally but neatly, with a hypothetical force; thus (a) in past or present time Exod 16:21 וְנָמָֽס׃ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְחַם‎ and the sun used to be warm, and it used to melt = and if (or when) the sun was warm, it melted, 33:10; 1Kin 18:10; Jer 18:4, 8 וְנִחַמְתִּ֫י וְֹשָׁב‎ = and if it turns, I repent, 20:9 (see RV); (β) in future time, Gen 44:22 ומת אביו ועזב‎ and he will leave his father, and he will die = and if he leaves his father, he will die, 33:13; 42:38; Exod 4:14; 12:13; 1Sam 16:2; 19:3; Ezek 33:3; 39:15 etc. (Dr§ 147-9, Ges§ 159. 2 e).

3 With a

voluntative (cohortative or jussive) וְ‎ expresses an intention, that or so that (an elegancy by which the too frequent use of לְמַעַן‎ or בַּעֲבוּר‎ is avoided): Exod 10:17 entreat God, וְיָסֵר‎ so may he remove (= that he may remove) this death, Gen 27:4 and bring it me וְאֹכֵ֑לָה‎ so let me eat (= that I may eat); and without the modal form being externally indicated, Exod 14:1 speak . . . וְיָשֻׁבוּ‎ that they return, 14:15; and often Sts. even of past time, as 1Kin 13:33 whom he would, he consecrated וִיהִי‎ that there might be priests of the high places, 2Kin 19:25; Isa 25:9 a Lam 1:19. After a negative, Psa 51:18 thou desirest not sacrifice, וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה‎ so [= in that case] would I give it (or, that I might give it), 55:13 וְאֶשָּׂא‎ so could I bear it (or, that I might bear it), Isa 53:2 RVm Num 23:19; Jer 5:28 RV. Sts. also before an imperative, Gen 12:2 and be (= that thou mayest be) a blessing, 2Sam 21:3 +. See more fully Dr§ 59-65, Ges§ 108. 2; 109. 2; 110. 2. (In Arabic with the subjunctive is used similarly: Wii. § 15 d.) A volunt. is also sometimes attached by וְ‎ to a preceding volunt. or imperative, so as to form a virtually hypothetical sentence, as Gen 42:18 וִחְיוּ עֲשׂוּ זֹאת‎ = if you do this, you shall live, 30:28; 34:12; Prov 3:9f. 4:4, 8; Isa 55:2: see Dr§ 152.

4 It expresses often an informal inference, or consequence, so, then, especially at the beginning of a speech: Gen 27:8; Psa 2:10 and often וְעַתָּה‎ now, therefore; וְלָמָּה‎ and וּמַדּוּעַ‎ why, then? Gen 29:25; Num 12:8; 16:3 +; Exod 2:20 וְאַיּוֺ‎ where, then, is he? Gen 34:21; 1Sam 15:14; 26:22 וְיַעֲבֹר‎ let, then, . . . come over, 2Sam 24:3; 2Kin 4:41 קֶמַח וּקְחוּ‎ then bring meal, Ezek 18:32. So the וְ‎ consecutive and the perfect, as Deut 2:4 וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם‎ take heed, therefore, 4:15; 7:9 וְיָָֽדַעְתָּ֫‎ know, therefore, 30:19; 1Sam 6:5; 1Kin 2:6; Ruth 3:9; Josh 15:19; Isa 40:6b (Dr§ 119 δ).

5 ו‎ introduces the predicate or apodosis: namely

a. וְ‎ consecutive and the Perfect — in answer to אִם‎ or כִּי‎ constantly, as Exod 19:5; 23:22 if thou hearkenest to my voice, וְאָֽיַבְתִּ֫י‎ then am I (= I will be) enemy to thy enemies (see Dr§ 136-8); after the casus pendens, 12:44 every servant that is bought for money, וּמַלְתָּ֫ה‎ thou shalt circumcise him, etc. Num 14:31; 24:24; 1Sam 25:27; 2Sam 14:10 he that spake unto thee, אֵלַי וַהֲבֵאתוֺ‎ so hast thou brought him (= thou shalt bring him) unto me, Isa 9:4; 56:6f. +; Exod 12:15; 31:14; Deut 17:12 +; after various time-determinations, as Gen 3:5 in the day of your eating from it וְנִפְקְחוּ‎ then shall your eyes be opened, Exod 16:6 וִידַעְתֶּם עֶרֶב‎ at even, then shall ye know, 16:7; 32:34; 2Sam 15:10; 1Kin 13:31 אֹתִי וּקְבַרְתֶּם בְּמוֺתִי‎ when I die, so ye shall bury me, etc., + often; after conjs., as כִּי‎ Gen 29:15, יַעַן‎ 1Kin 20:28; Isa 3:16f., תַּחַת‎ 60:15, etc., (see Dr§ 123).

b. וַּ ‎ consecutive and the imperfect (but much less frequently than the perfect), as Gen 30:30 the little that thou hadst, וַיִּפְרֹץ‎ it hath increased, Exod 9:21; 2Sam 4:10; 1Kin 9:20f. 15:13 +; after time-determinations, Gen 22:4 on the third day וַיִּשָּׂא‎ then Abraham lifted up his eyes, 19:15; 27:34; 37:18; 1Sam 6:6; 12:8; Isa 6:1; Hosea 11:1 when Israel was a child, וָאֹהֲבֵהוּ‎ then I loved him, +; occasionally after conjunctions, as כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ Exod 16:34, יַעַן‎ 1Sam 15:23, לְמַעַן‎ Isa 45:4, אִם‎ Psa 59:16 (Dr§ 127).

c. in other cases (not 'consecutive') — all more or less uncommon: namely a. וְ‎ closely joined to the imperfect Gen 13:9 if to the left, וְאֵימִינָה‎ then I will take the right (compare 2Sam 12:8) Exod 12:3 on the 10th of the month וְיִקְחוּ‎ then let them take, Num 16:5; Isa 43:4; Hosea 4:6; 10:10; Psa 69:33; Job 15:17; 2Sam 22:41; Prov 23:24 Kt (Dr§ 125); β. separated from the verb, Exod 8:22; Lev 7:16 יֵאָכֵל וְהַנּוֺתָר וּמִמָּחֳרָת‎ and on the morrow, then the remainder shall be eaten, Josh 3:3; 1Kin 8:32; Isa 8:7; 48:7; Job 14:7; 20:18; b 23:12; 25:5; 32:14 +; γ. without a verb, Gen 40:9 וְהִנֵּה בַּחֲלֹמִי‎ in my dream, behold, a vine was before me, 40:16; 2Sam 23:3f.; Prov 10:25, and the extreme cases 2Sam 15:34 thy father's slave, מֵאָז וַאֲנִי‎ I was that of old, — but now עַבְדְּךָ וַאֲנִי‎ well, I will be thine, Isa 34:12 (si vera lectio), Job 4:6b דְּרָכֶיךָ וְתֹם תִּקְוָָֽתְךָ‎ thy confidence — it is the uprightness of thy ways, 36:26 חֵקֶר וְלֹא שָׁנָיו מִסְמַּר‎ Ges. seine Jahre, da ist kein Zählen (compare Dr§ 124-5, 128-9). — With 4, 5 compare the Arabic , Wi. § 366 b, 367 c; ii. § 187; Dr§ 185 end.

מעזן.def:
H4581. maoz

or mauz or maoz or mauz מָעוֺז‎ noun masculineJudg 6:26 place or means of safety, protection (ᵑ0‎ suffixes as if from עזז‎, but probably erroneous, compare BuhlLex 13 Ges§ 85k); — ׳מ‎ absolute 6:26 +, construct Isa 30:2 +; suffix מָעוּזִי‎ 2Sam 22:33 (but read הַמְּאַזְּרֵנִי‎ as || Psa 18:33), מָעוּזִּי‎ 31:3 +, מָעֻזִּי‎ Isa 27:5 +, מָעוּזּוֺ‎ Psa 52:9 +, מָעֻזֹּה‎ Dan 11:10, etc. (read probably מְעוֺזִּי‎, etc.); plural מָעֻזִּים‎ 11:38; 11:39, suffix מָעֻזְּנֶיהָ‎ Isa 23:11, read מָעֻזֶּיהָ‎ (Ges§ 20o CheHeb.Hpt. and others; strike out dagesh forte in all, see above); —

1 literally place of safety Judg 6:26, hence (c. collateral idea of strength, as if from עזז‎ = fastness Isa 23:11, 14 (in 23:14 CheHeb.Hpt. proposes מְחוֺזְכֶם‎ your city), Ezek 24:25; 30:15; Dan 11:7, 10, 19, הַמּ ׳הַמִּקְדָּשׁ‎ 11:31, מָעֻזִּים מִבְצְרֵי‎ 11:39; ׳מ הַיָּם‎ i.e. harbour Isa 23:4, but strike out O1 Du CheHpt.; ׳מ מֵאוֺיֵב‎ Nahum 3:11; compare מ ׳עָרֵי‎ Isa 17:9.

2. a. figurative, of God (׳י‎) as refuge Nahum 1:7; Psa 27:1; 31:5; 37:39; 52:9; Isa 25:4 (twice in verse); Joel 4:16, ׳י וּמְנוּסִי וּמָעֻזִּי עֻזִּי‎ Jer 16:19, ׳מ מְשִׁיחוֺ יְשׁוּעוֺת‎ Psa 28:8 (|| עָזֿ‎); so מ ׳צוּר‎ Isa 17:10; Psa 31:3, מ ׳אֱלֹהֵי‎ 43:2; also בְּמָעֻזִּי יַחֲזֵק‎ Isa 27:5 let him lay hold of my refuge (me as refuge); cf . י ׳חֶדְוַת מָעֻזְּכֶם הִיא‎ Neh 8:10, ׳מ י דֶּרֶךְ ׳לַתֹּם‎ Prov 10:29.

b. of a heathen god, מָעֻזִּים אֱלוֺהַּ‎ Dan 11:38 (read מְחֹזִים‎ cities CheIsa 23:1,Heb.Hpt.).

3 figurative of human protection, ׳מ מַּרְעֹה‎ Isa 30:2-3,(both || מִצְרַיִם צֵּל‎); מ ׳אֶפְרַיִם ראֹשִׁי‎ Psa 60:9 = 108:9, i.e. my helmet; also (of angel) Dan 11:1 (|| מַחֲזִיק‎).

עֲוִיל‎ see II. עול‎. below

מעט.def:
H4591. maat

[מָעַט‎] verb be or become small, diminished, few (Late Hebrew, Talmud, id.; Arabic is to be without hair on the body) —

Qal Imperfect יִמְעַט‎ Exod 12:4, 2masculine plural תִּמְעָ֑טוּ‎ Jer 29:6, 3masculine plural יִמְעָ֑טוּ‎ Isa 21:17 +, וַיִּמְעֲטוּ‎ Psa 107:39; Infinitive מְעֹט‎ Lev 25:16; — Exod 12:4 מִשֶּׂה מִהְיוֺת הַבַּיִת אִסיִֿמְעַט‎ if the house be too small for a lamb; Neh 9:32 כָּלהַֿתְּלָאָה אֵת לְפָנֶיךָ אַליִֿמְעַט‎ (compare Ges§ 117l); of a people, Jer 29:6 וְאַלתִּֿמְעָ֑טוּ שָׁם וּרְבוּ‎ and become not few, 30:19 יִמְעָ֔טוּ וְלֹא וְהִרְבִּתִים‎, Isa 21:17; Psa 107:39; Prov 13:11 יִמְעָ֑ט מֵהֶבֶל הוֺן‎ diminishes (opposed to יַרְבֶּה‎); Lev 25:16 הַשָּׁנִים מְעֹט וּלְפִי‎ according to the fewness of the years.

Pi`el become few (Ges§ 52k), Perfect3plural Eccl 12:3 מִעֵ֔טוּ כִּי הַטֹּחֲנוֺת וּבָֽטְלוּ‎.

Hiph`il Perfect3feminine singular consecutive וְהִמְעִ֫יטָה‎ (Ges§ 49k), Lev 26:22, 1singular with suffix וְהִמְעַטְתִּים‎ Ezek 29:15; Imperfect2masculine singular תַּמְעִיט‎ Lev 25:16, תַּמְעִטֵ֫נִי‎ Jeremiah 10:34, 2feminine singular תַּמְעִ֫יטִי‎ 2Kin 4:3, etc.; — make small or few, diminish:

a. Lev 26:22 (of the sword) אֶתְכֶם וְהִמְעִ֫יטָה‎, Ezek 29:15 וְהִמְעַטְתִּים‎, Jer 10:24 תַּמְעִטֵנִי מֶּןֿ אַלבְּֿאַמְּךָ‎ lest thou make me (the people) small, Psa 107:38 יַמְעִיט לֹא וּבְהֶמְתָּם‎; Lev 25:16 מִקְנָתוֺ תַּמְעִיט הַשָּׁנִים מְעֹט וּלְפִי‎ according to the smallness (fewness) of the years, thou shalt make small its price, Num 26:54 נַחֲלָתוֺ תַּמְעִיט וְלַמְעַט נַחֲלָתוֺ תַּרְבֶּה לָרַב‎ and to the small (few) thou shalt make small his inheritance (so 33:54).

b. qualifying an action (sometimes to be understood from the context), Exod 16:17 וְהַמַּמְעִיט הַמַּרְבֶּה וַיִּלְקְטוּ‎ and they gathered, he that made much, and he that made little (that is לִלְקֹט‎), 16:18; Num 11:32 אסף הממעיט חמרים עשׂרה‎, 2Kin 4:3 אַלתַּֿמְעִיטִי רֵקִים כֵּלִים‎ empty vessels make not few (that is, in borrowing); Exod 30:15 וגו ׳לָתֵת הַשָּׁ֑קֶל מִמַּחֲצִית יַמְעִיט לֹא וְהַדַּל יַרְבֶּה לֹא הֶעָשִׁיר‎ shall not diminish from the half shekel to give, i.e. shall not give less, Num 35:8 תַּמְעִיטוּ הַמְעַט וּמֵאֵת תַּרְבּוּ הָרַב מֵאֵת‎ and from the few ye shall make few (that is לָתֵת‎), i.e. ye shall give few (cities).

מעיל.def:
H4598. meil

מעים.def:
H4578. meeh

[מֵעֶה‎] noun masculineIsa 16:11 only

plural internal organs, inward parts (intestines, bowels), belly (Late Hebrew id.; Aramaic מַעֲיָא מְעָא,‎, , ; Arabic ; Ethiopic ; — on form compare LagBN 156 BaZMG xiii. 1888, 345); — plural [מֵעִים‎] construct מְעֵי‎ Psa 71:6 3t.; suffix מֵעַי‎ 2Sam 16:11 9t., מֵעָ֑י‎ Psa 22:15; 40:9; מֵעֶיךָ‎ Gen 15:4 6t.; מֵעַיִךְ‎ 25:23; Num 5:22; מֵעָיו‎ 2Sam 20:10 5t.; מֵעֵיהֶם‎ Ezek 7:19; —

1 literally:

a. אַ֫רְצָה מֵעָיו וַיִּשְׁמֹּךְ‎ 2Sam 20:10 and he poured out his inward parts on the ground (through a wound); compare מ ׳מַחֲלֵה‎2Chr 21:15, 18, מ ׳יָָֽצְאוּ‎ 21:15; 21:19.

b. as digestive organs, but without precision, nearly = stomach, belly, Job 20:14; Ezek 3:3 (|| בֶּטֶן‎), 7:19 (|| נֶפֶשׁ‎; both with מָלֵא‎), Num 5:22; so of fish that swallowed Jonah Jonah 2:1; 2:2.

2 source of procreation: ׳מִמּ יצא אשׁר‎ (said of offspring) Gen 15:4 (JE), 2Sam 7:12 (|| זַרְעֲךָ‎), 16:11; מ ׳צֶאֱצָאֵי‎ Isa 48:19 (|| id.); מ ׳מִיצִיאֵי‎2Chr 32:21.

3 = womb, יִמָּרֵ֑דוּ מִמֵּעַיִח לְאֻמִּים שְׁנֵי‎ Gen 25:23 (J; || בֶּטֶן‎), compare Isa 49:1 (|| id.), Psa 71:6 (|| id.), Ruth 1:11.

4 in General = inwards, inward part, מ בְּתוֺךְ נָמֵס ֗֗֗ ׳לִבִּי‎ Psa 22:15, compare מ בְּתוֺךְ ׳תּוֺרָֽתְךָ‎ 40:9.

5 figurative = seat of emotions: pity, Isa 16:11 (|| קֶרֶב‎); of God's compassion, Jer 31:20 (|| רחם‎; in both subject of verb הָמוּ‎); מֵעֶיךָ הֲמוֺן‎ Isa 63:15 (|| רַחֲמֶיךָ‎); distress, Jer 4:19 (twice in verse) (|| חֳמַרְמָרוּ מֵעַי לֵב,‎ Lam 1:20 (|| לֵב‎), 2:11 (|| כָּבֵד‎ liver); רֻתְּחוּ מֵעַי‎ Job 30:27 (dubious, see Bu); love, עָלָיו הָמוּ מֵעַי‎ Song 5:4.

6 the external belly, שֵׁן עֶשֶׁת מֵעָיו‎ Song 5:14.

a. son of Nahor by his concubine רְאוּמָה‎ Gen 22:22 (J), ancestor of people see

3. b. father of חָנָן‎, a hero of David 1Chr 11:43.

c. Simeonite name 1Chr 27:16.

2. feminine ᵐ5‎ Μ(ο)ωχα, Μααχα, etc.:

a. Geshurite princess, wife of David, mother of Absalom, 2Sam 3:3 = 1Chr 3:2.

3. of a people, ᵐ5‎ Μοοχα, Μωχα, Μα(α)χα; dwelling west of Bashan, near Soba, and Geshur (compare especially adjective, of a people below), 2Sam 10:6, 8 = 1Chr 19:7, מ ׳אֲרַם‎ 19:6 (compare Gen 22:24 above); = מַעֲכָת‎ Josh 13:13 (+ גְּשׁוּר‎), ᵐ5‎ ὀ Μαχατει, Μαχαθι. — מַעֲכָה בֵּית אָבֵל‎ see below בַּיִת‎, p. 112 above, and אָבֵל‎, p. 5.

verb Qal, Hiph`il; noun, 10.

מַעֲשֶׂה‎233 noun masculineGen 20:9 deed, work; — absolute ׳מ‎ 44:15 +, construct מַעֲשֵׂה‎ Isa 5:12 +; suffix מַעֲשֵׂהוּ‎ Judg 13:12 +, etc.; plural מַעֲשִׂים‎ Gen 20:9 +; construct מַעֲשֵׂי‎ Jer 1:16 +; suffix מַעֲשָׂיו‎ 1Sam 19:4 (or singular, so Dr) +, etc.; — often accusative of congnate meaning with verb with עשׂה‎; —

1. a.-1deed, thing done by man Num 16:28 (JE), 1Kin 13:11; Isa 26:12; — b.-1work, labour, husbandry Exod 23:16 (E), Gen 5:29 (J), Judg 19:16,

c. deed(s), work(s) of ׳י‎, especially in deliverance and in judgment, Judg 2:7, 10; Josh 24:31 (D), Psa 33:4 21t., + ׳מ יָדָיו‎ etc. Isa 5:12; Psa 28:5; 92:5 4t.; ׳מ הָאֱלֹהִים‎ in General Eccl 7:13; 8:17; 11:5; compare 3:11.

2. a.-1work, thing made, by man, ׳מ אֹפֶה‎

b. work (made by) God Exod 32:16 (E); especially (poetry and late), of created things, Psa 103:22; 104:24 4t. Psalms; ׳מ אֶצְבְּעֹתֶיךָ‎ 8:4, ׳מ יָרֶיךָ‎ 102:26 (both of heavens), compare 19:2 (heavenly bodies), 8:7 (animals); of man Job 14:15; 34:19, compare מַעֲשֵׂהוּ כָּלאַֿנְשֵׁי לָדַעַת‎ 37:7 (but read probably ᵑ9 אנשׁים‎ Ol Di and others); of nation Isa 19:25; 60:21; 64:7; of weights Prov 16:11 (but read perhaps הַמֶּלֶךְ‎) for ׳י‎ Gr Toy).

c. product of olive-tree, ׳מ זַיִת‎ Hab 3:17; figurative product of righteousness Isa 32:17.

מפעל.def:
H5704. ad

III. עַד‎, in poetry עֲדֵי‎ ( Num 24:20, 24; Psa 104:23; 147:6; Job 7:4; 20:5, and in עַד עֲדֵי‎ Isa 26:4; 65:18; Psa 83:18; 92:8; 132:12; 132:14:compare עֲלֵי אֱלֵי,‎),

preposition as far as, even to, up to, until, while (Aramaic עד‎, Sabean עדי עד,‎, MordtmZMG xxx (1876), 27; DHMxxxvii (1883), 414, Assyrian adi Dl§ 81 a (Arabic is except); perh akin to pass on, advance to, Köii. 304, 309: עֲדֵי‎ probably from ground-form ±¦d¦y, Ol428, 431 Köii. 309 ff.; but LagSym. ii. 101-3, Mitth. i. 231 f., as plur. like אַחֲרֵי‎); — with suffix עָדַי‎ Num 23:18 +, עָדֶיךָ‎ Micah 4:8 +, etc., עָֽדיֵכֵם‎ Job 32:12; 2Kin 9:18 עַדהֵֿם‎ occurs; — as far as, even to (differing from אֶל‎ in that the limit is included, as in Arabic FlKl. Schr. i. 402 f.):

I. preposition 1. of space; —

a. Gen 11:31 חרן עד ויבאו‎ as far as Haran, 12:6; 13:3, 12 + often, Isa 8:8 יגעַ צואר עד‎, 15:4 קולם נשׁמע יהץ עד‎, 25:12; 26:5; Psa 36:6 שׁחקים עד אמונתך‎, 69:2 נפשׁ עד מים דאו‎ (compare Jonah 2:6; Micah 1:9; Jer 4:10, 18), Jer 90:3דַּכָּא עַד אֱנוֺשׁ תָּשֵׁד‎ Job 11:7, etc.; pregnantly Psa 118:27 וגו עַד חָג ׳אִסְדוּ‎ bind . . . (and lead) up to . . .; Isa 57:9 מֵרָחוק עַד‎ even to afar (מִן‎

1c); with the goal a person, Exod 22:8 שְׁנֵיהֶם דְבַר יָבאֹ האלהים עד‎, 1Sam 9:9; Psa 65:3 יָבאֹוּ כָלבָּֿשָׂר עָדֶיךָ‎ Isa 45:24; Job 4:5, י עַד ׳שׁוּב‎ Hosea 14:2 al. (see שׁוּב‎, stronger than אֶליֿ ׳שׁוּב‎); in poetry Num 24:20 אֹבֵד עֲדֵי וְאַחֲדִיתוֺ‎ shall be even unto destruction, shall issue in destruction, 24:24; rarely with verbs of attending, עַד הֶאֱזִין‎ 23:18, עַד הִתְבּוֺנֵן‎ Job 32:12; 38:18 (usually אֶל‎). Before another perp., 1Sam 7:11 ל מִתַּחַת ׳עַד‎ 1Kin 4:12 מֵעַל עַד ל, מֵעֵבֶר ׳עַד‎ Ezek 41:20, לִפְנֵי עַד‎ Est 4:2, and even (si vera. l.) אְלֵיהֶם עַד‎ 2Kin 9:20:compare נֶגֶד עַד‎ Neh 3:16, 26, נֹכַח עַד‎ Judg 19:10 +.

b. In the combination (וְ)עַד ֗֗֗ מִן‎, as Gen 10:19 עַזָּה עַד ֗֗֗ מצידון‎ from Sidon . . . as far as Gaza + often (see מן‎

5a); and idiomatic, not of actual space, but of class of objects, to express the idea of both... and, as Gen 19:4 זָקִן וְעַד מִנַּעַר‎ from young to old (inclusively) = both young and old (see מִן‎

5b); without מִן‎, even to = including, Lev 11:42; Num 8:4 even to (i. e. including) it base and its flower, compare 1Sam 18:4.

2 Of time:

a. (a) even to, until Gen 8:5 even to the 10th month, Exod 12:6 unto the 14th day, etc., 12:15; 12:18, etc.; היום עד‎ unto this day, Gen 19:37-38, הזה היום עד‎ 26:33; Genesis 32:33, both + often; יום עד‎ followed by infinitive Exod 40:37; Josh 6:10; Judg 18:30; בקר עד‎ till morning, Exod 12:10 + (15 t.), הבקר עד‎ 16:23 + (11 t.); so (ה)ערב עד‎ 18:13-14, +, in poetry ערב עֲרֵי‎ Psa 104:23; עוֺלָם עַד‎ Gen 13:15 + often; מְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע עַד‎ 2Kin 4:35; וָדוֺר דּוֺר עַד‎ Isa 13:20; see also בְּלִי‎, and בִּלְתִּי‎, near the end and followed by another preposition, Lev 23:16 הַשַּׁבָּת מִמָּחֳרַת עַד‎, Neh 13:9 הַשַּׁבָּת אַחַר עַד‎. With the force of against, Judg 6:31 הַבֹּקֶר עַד יוּמַת‎; compare (b) end. (b) followed by infinitive, both of past time, as Gen 8:7; Genesis 32:35 הַשַּׁחַר עֲלוֺת עַד‎, 33:3; 34:5, and especially future time, as 3:19 שׁוּבְךָ עַד‎ until thy returning, 19:22; 27:45; Deut 7:20, 23; 20:20; 22:2; 28:20, 22, — both + often; compare בּוֺשׁ עַד‎ Judg 3:25 +; ֗֗֗ תֹּם עַד‎ Lev 25:29 10t.; תֻּמָּם עַד‎ Deut 2:15 +; כַּלֵּה עַד‎ 2Kin 13:17, 19; Ezek 19:14; כַּלּוֺתָ(םׅ עַד‎ 1Sam 15:18; Jer 9:15 +; הַבֹּקֶר אוֺר עַד‎ Judg 16:2 +; also in אֹתָם הִשְׁמִדְךָ עַד‎ Deut 7:24 (compare 28:48; Josh 11:14; 1Kin 15:29; 2Kin 3:25; 10:17; 24:20 [|| Jer 52:3 הִשְׁלִיכוֺ‎]; on the anomalous ׳הִ‎, see Dr, read probably ׳הַ‎); and most probably compare Köiii. 583) in שָׂרִיד (לָהֶם) לוֺ הִשְׁאִיר בִּלְתִּי עַד‎ Deut 3:3 (see Dr), + 5 t. (see above), read probably הַשְׁאִיר‎. With the force of towards the end of, against, especially in בֹּאָ(םׅ עַד‎, Gen 43:25; Exod 22:25; Num 10:21 בֹּאָם עַד המשׁכן את והקימו‎ used to set up the tabernacle against their coming, 2Kin 16:11; Ezek 33:22; compare 2Sam 17:22. Elliptical Judg 16:2 וַהֲרַגְנוּהוּ הַבֹּקֶד אוֺד עַד‎ (wait) till the morning dawn, and we slay him! (GFM; Dr§ 115). (c) with various adverbs of time. (q. v.) as עַתָּה עַד כֵּן, עַד כֹּה, עַד הֵנָּה, עַד מָתַי, עַד עַדמָֿה, אָנָה, עַד‎, compare פְעָמִים כַּמֶּה עַד‎ (see מָה‎

4b). (d) to suffest also degree (compare

3), מָקוֺם אֵין עַד‎ until there is no place Isa 5:8, מִסְמָּר אֵין עַד‎ Psa 40:13; Job 5:9; 9:10; compare Lev 26:18 וְאִםעַֿדאֵֿלֶּה‎ and if even up to these things, even the end of all these punishment, you do not hearken to me.

b. During (rare; prop, as far as the limit indicated, including the time previous, compare ἔως: so often Aramaic עַד‎, , while), 2Kin 9:22 what is peace אִיזֶבֶל זְנוּנֵי עַד‎ during, etc.,? Job 20:5 רָ֑גַע עֲדֵי‎ during a moment; followed by infinitive Judg 3:26 הִתְמַהְמְהָם עַד‎ during their delaying, Exod 33:22; Job 7:19 רֻקִּי בִּלְעִי עַד‎ Jonah 4:2.

3 Of degree, to suggest a higher or the highest; as מְאֹד עַד‎ even to muchness, i.e. exceedingly (see מְאֹד‎), מְהֵרָה עַד‎ even to haste Psa 147:15; Est 5:6 וְתֵעָשׂ הַמַּלְכוּת עַדחֲֿצִי וּמַהבֻּֿקָּשָׁתֵךְ‎, 5:3; 7:2. See also לְ עַד‎, below. With a negative, to express not even as much as, Deut 2:5 רָ֑גֶל כַּף מִדְרַךְ עַד מארצם לכם אתן לא‎, and with אֶחָד‎, Exod 9:7 עַדאֶֿחָד ֗֗֗ מֵת לֹא‎, simil. 14:28; Judg 4:16; 2Sam 17:22 (read אֶחָד‎ for ׃אַחַד‎ see Dr). Sts. almost = Latin adeo, 1Sam 2:5 (si vera lectio) שׁבעה ילדה עֲקָרָה עַד‎ even to the barren, she hath borne seven, i.e. even the barren hath, etc., Job 25:5 יאהיל ולא עדיָֿרֵחַ הן‎, Hag 2:19. In comparisons, to the degree of, even like (rare), Nahum 1:10 סְבֻכִים סִירִים עַד‎ (text dubious) entangled even like thorns, 1Chr 4:27 יהודה בני עד הִרְבּוּ לא‎ did not multiply to the degree of (i.e.like), etc. compare. 2Sam 23:19 בָא לֹא הַשְּׁלשָׁה עַד‎ did not attain (in prowess) unto the three.

II. conjunction 1. until; —

a אֲשֶׁר עַד‎ until that: (a) with perfect, of past time, Exod 32:20 דָּק אשׁר עד ויטחן‎ (Deut 9:21), 2:14 עָבַרְנוּ אשׁר עד‎, Josh 3:17; 8:26; Judg 4:24; 1Kin 10:7 (2Chr 9:6), 2Kin 17:20, 23; 21:16; with suggestion of degree, 1Sam 30:4 (followed byאֵין‎), 1Kin 17:17; rarely of future time (the 'future perfect,' Dr§ 17), 2Sam 17:13 (of degree), Ezek 34:21 So -שֶׁ עַד‎ (often in Late Hebrew; see שֶׁ‎) Judg 5:7; Song 3:4 (twice in verse); כִּי עַד‎ Gen 26:13 מְאֹד כִּיגָֿדַל עַד‎, 41:49; 2Sam 23:10; 2Chr 26:15; and (of future time) אִם אֲשֶׁר עַד‎ Gen 28:15; Num 32:17; Isa 6:11. b. עַד‎ alone, until: (a) with perfect, of past time, Josh 2:22; 4:23 עַדעָֿבַרְנוּ‎, 1Sam 20:41 הִגְדִּיל דָּוִד עַד‎, 2Sam 21:10; 1Kin 11:16; Ezek 28:15; of the future (rare), 2Kin 7:3 מָ֑תְנוּ עַד‎, Ezek 39:15; Dan 11:36 זָ֑עַם כָּלָה עַד‎. So סִם עַד‎ (of the future), Gen 24:19, 33; Isa 30:17; Ruth 2:21. (b) with imperfect, of future time, 1Sam 1:22 (elliptic: compare Judg 16:2,

12a (b) end), Isa 22:14; 26:20; 32:15; 62:1, 7; Psa 57:2; 71:18; Job 27:5 +; of the past (rare), Exod 15:16 עמך יעבור עד‎, 15:16; Josh 10:13 (poetry) אוֺיְבָיו גּוֺי יִקֹּם עַד‎, Psa 73:17. — N.B. a. with perfect, 1Sam 14:19 שׁאול דִּבֶּר עד‎ while Saul spake.

or miqqedash מִקְדָּשׁ‎ noun masculineAmos 7:9 sacred place, sanctuary; — ׳מ‎ Exod 25:8 +; מִקְּדָשׁ‎ 15:17 (Ges§ 20h Köii. 1, 471); construct מִקְדַּשׁ‎ Lev 16:33 +; suffix מִקְדָּשִׁי‎ 20:3 +, etc., מִקְדְּשׁוֺ‎ Num 18:29 (Köii. 1, 97); plural מִקְדָּשִׁים‎ Ezek 21:7, construct מִקְדְּשֵׁי‎ Jer 51:51 2t.; suffix מִקְדָּשַׁי‎ Lev 21:23; מְקַדְשֵׁיהֶם‎ Ezek 7:24 (on anomalous pointing see Ew§ 215 a Hi-Sm; but probably

Pi`el Participle was in mind, Ges§ 93oo Anm.; < read מִקְדְּשֵׁיהֶם‎); etc.; —

2 of the nations: Moab Isa 16:12 plural of Tyre Ezek 28:18 (Co Toy [not Berthol Krae] read קָדְשְׁךָ‎ thy sanctity).

3 tabernacle and its precincts Exod 25:8 (P) +; הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִקְדַּשׁ‎ Lev 16:33, plural 21:23.

4 temple and precincts 1Chr 22:19; Isa 63:18; Psa 74:7 +; מִקְדָּשָׁם בֵּית‎2Chr 36:17, הבית מקדשׁ‎ Ezek 48:21, מ ׳מְכוֺן‎ Dan 8:11; plural of many sacred places in and about the temple. י בית ׳מִקְדְּשֵׁי‎ Jer 51:51; אֵל מִקְדְּשֵׁי‎ Psa 73:17. Doubtful are: מִמִּקְדָּשֶׁיךָ‎ Psalm 68:36 (ᵐ5‎ ἐν τοῖς ὁσίοις αὐτοῦ ᵑ9‎ de sanctuario; SS מִקְדָּשֶׁ֑ךָ‎); מִקְדָּשִׁים‎ Ezek 21:7 (ᵐ5‎ Co Berthol Buhl מִקְדָּשָׁם‎; Toy Krae מִקְדָּשֶׁיהָ‎; || יְרוּשָׁלַםִ‎); לַמִּקְדָּשׁ וּמִקְדָּשׁ‎ 45:4b (Co, after לְקָדְשָׁם מִפְקָד ᵐ5,‎ [לְבָֽתֵּי‎]; Toy וּלְמִגְרָשִׁים‎ [לְבָֽתִּים‎], compare Krae לְמִגְרָשׁ‎).

5 ׳י‎ will become ׳לְמ‎ for his people Ezek 11:16 (BrMP 268), so apparently Isa 8:14 (but gloss Du CheHpt Marti; LagSemitic i. 16 מִקָּשׁ‎ i.e. stumbling-block [he compare Syriac strike]).

מָקוֺר‎ noun masculineZech 13:1 spring, fountain (apparently originally well); — absolute ׳מ‎ 13:1; Prov 25:26; construct מְקוֺר‎ Jer 2:13 +, מְקֹר‎ Lev 12:7; 20:18; suffix מְקוֺרוֺ‎ Hosea 13:15, etc.; —

a; figurative, of חַיִּים ׳מ מַיִם ׳י,‎ Jer 2:13; 17:13, compare ׳מ חַיִּים‎ Psa 36:10; ׳מ חַיִּים‎ (more Generally), Prov 10:11; 13:14; 14:27; 16:22 + 18:4 (so read for ᵐ5 ׳מ חָכְמָה‎ Hebrew Manuscripts Toy).
